1	# Whodunit
2	
3	41 commits since it last worked. Which one did it?
4	
5	Whodunit answers two questions about an AI agent that used to work and now fails: which commit broke it, and why that commit was made. Then it fixes the commit, proves the fix by replaying the failures, and counts what the breakage cost.
6	
7	It was built for neatHack between 10 and 12 October 2026. `hackathon.md` is the dated build log, including the parts that went wrong.
8	
9	## Why plain bisect is not enough
10	
11	`git bisect` assumes a bad commit fails every time. Agents do not behave that way. A prompt change might break one run in three, and a commit that is perfectly fine might still fail one run in twenty. Test a bad commit once, see it pass, and bisect walks off in the wrong direction without telling you.
12	
13	Whodunit replays the failing inputs against suspect commits and keeps a probability for each suspect being the first bad one. It names a commit only when it is 95% sure. If the replay budget runs out first, it hands back the suspects still in the lineup with their probabilities.
14	
15	How well that works is measured two ways. [eval/sealed](eval/sealed/README.md) is five regressions planted by a separate session with a sealed answer key: three were named inside 120 replays, all five after more, and no commit was wrongly accused. [eval/simulator](eval/simulator/README.md) is simulated cases with a known culprit. The short version: when good commits never fail, plain bisect with repeats is cheaper. When good commits fail 5% of the time on their own, it falls apart and the statistical bisect does not.
16	
17	## How a case runs
18	
19	A case is a small TOML file: a symptom, the failing inputs with what each should have produced, the last good ref and the first bad ref. One command runs all of it:
20	
21	```bash
22	uv run whodunit investigate cases/whole-history.toml --from-traffic refund-agent
23	```
24	
25	It stops only when it needs the owner's ruling. Each step is also a command of its own (`lineup`, `brief`, `ruling`, `fix`, `damages`, `open-case`), and each adds to one record next to the case file. The case file page is drawn from that record.
26	
27	On the refund agent's real history, 57 commits grown by a separate coding session, that command named the culprit at 99.8% after 20 replays, quoted the request that caused it, patched it, proved the patch on 30 clean replays and counted 120.00 in refunds that had gone to the wrong people. [evidence/casefile-whole-history.png](evidence/casefile-whole-history.png) is the page it wrote.
28	
29	0. Before any replay, two things narrow the field. entire-graph says which commits could not have reached the agent (a README edit, a helper script the agent never calls), and those start with less suspicion. And ordinary runs that already asked what the case asks are evidence that is already paid for.
30	1. The lineup checks every suspect commit out into its own git worktree and replays the case inputs there. Each replay is a real run of the agent, traced to neatroots and tagged with the commit and the case. A commit that will not build is skipped, as `git bisect skip` does.
31	2. The motive comes from Entire. A commit made by a coding agent carries a checkpoint, and the checkpoint holds the session. Whodunit finds the prompt that led to the commit and what the coding agent did next.
32	3. The brief is written by a model from the culprit's diff, that slice of the session, and a failing run set against a passing one. Every sentence has to cite a span, a commit or a checkpoint that is really in the evidence. Sentences that do not are cut.
33	4. The ruling is the owner's. It is asked once per kind of change (a prompt change, a tool change, a dependency) and remembered under `rulings/`.
34	5. The fix is a revert or a patch on a local branch. It is proven only when its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit, at 95%, which takes about 30 clean replays. A patch that is not proven is tried once more with its failures in view, and after that the culprit is reverted. The case is kept under `cases/` as a regression test that `whodunit check` can replay against any ref.
35	6. The damages are counted from the traces: how many runs went bad since the culprit, what they cost in tokens, and what they cost the shop, read from the refund tool's spans.
36	
37	Whodunit never pushes, opens a pull request or writes to anyone's finance model by itself. Those stay with the owner.
38	
39	## Try it
40	
41	You need Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git and a running neatroots.
42	
43	```bash
44	uv sync
45	uv run pytest -m "not slow"                    # the fast tests, no model and no keys
46	
47	# A throwaway repo with 20 commits, the refund agent and a planted bug:
48	uv run python tests/planted.py /tmp/planted
49	uv run python victims/refund-agent/fake_llm.py &
50	uv run whodunit lineup /tmp/planted/case.toml --repo /tmp/planted --method plain
51	```
52	
53	Add `flaky-lookup 40 27` to the `planted.py` line for 40 commits with a bug at commit 27 that fails about one run in three, and drop `--method plain` to use the statistical bisect.
54	
55	`uv run python -m whodunit.simulate --out eval/simulator` regenerates the simulator charts, and `uv run whodunit casebook` rewrites every case file and the index at `cases/index.html`.
56	
57	## What is in here
58	
59	- `whodunit/` is the tool. `lineup.py` holds both bisects, `replay.py` the worktree runner, `motive.py` the Entire lookups, `brief.py` the evidence and the brief, `ruling.py`, `fix.py` and `damages.py` the closing steps, and `casefile/` the page.
60	- `victims/refund-agent/` is the agent under investigation. It started as the `refund-agent` example that ships with neatroots, which is licensed under Apache-2.0. The licence is in that folder and the changes are listed in its README.
61	- `eval/simulator/` has the accuracy curves, the tables behind them and what they show.
62	- `tests/planted.py` builds histories with a known culprit. The tests and the demo use the same builder.
63	- `AGENTS.md` is the working brief for anyone writing code here.
64	
65	## Models and keys
66	
67	Keys live in `.env`, which git ignores. `.env.example` lists them. The code that needs a key reads the file itself.
68	
69	Replays of the refund agent use a scripted model by default and cost nothing. `REFUND_LLM=gateway` or `REFUND_LLM=own` switches them to a real model. Keep one model for the whole of a case, because a model change in the middle would look like a regression.
70	
71	The brief and the patch use `WHODUNIT_LLM`: `gateway`, `own`, `agent` for a coding agent in headless mode, or `none` for a fixed template with no model.
72	
73	## What it does not do yet
74	
75	- The statistical bisect assumes one change point. Two regressions in the same range will confuse it.
76	- A replay that times out counts as a failure, so a badly overloaded machine can frame an innocent commit.
77	- Damages are estimates from token counts and list prices.
78	- The model-written patch has been through one real case, a prompt regression on a planted history. That is not many.
79	- One of the five sealed cases is still open. Two patches improved it and neither brought it back to baseline, and the revert conflicts with later commits.
80	- The damages in the shop's currency depend on a tool span named `issue_refund`, so that part is specific to this agent.
81	- About one coding session in nine lost its Entire checkpoint while the history was grown. For those commits the motive falls back to the commit message.

1	# Whodunit working brief
2	
3	Whodunit finds the commit that broke an AI agent. It shows what that commit was asked to do, fixes it, proves the fix, and reports what the breakage cost. The pitch in one line: "41 commits since it last worked. Which one did it?"
4	
5	This is the brief for whoever writes code here, human or coding agent. Read it before changing anything.
6	
7	## Sessions in this repo are published
8	
9	Entire records every coding session in this repo and the repo is public, so the whole transcript of a session can be read by anyone. Treat everything typed, read or printed during a session as public.
10	
11	- Keys live in `.env`, which git ignores. Never print a value from it, never paste one into a prompt, and never open it with a tool that echoes its contents. Load it inside the code that needs it.
12	- Do not open private notes, mail, chat logs or any file outside this repo from a session here. If the work seems to need one, stop and ask the owner.
13	- Email and phone redaction is switched on in `.entire/settings.json`. After the first commit, read the checkpoint with `entire checkpoint explain --transcript` before anything is pushed.
14	- Never run `entire enable` with `--import-history`. It would pull older sessions from this folder into the public record.
15	
16	## How one case runs
17	
18	1. Read neatlogs and neatroots to get the failing runs and the time the failures began.
19	2. List the suspect commits between the last good ref and the first bad one.
20	3. Replay the failing inputs against suspect commits in git worktrees. Agent failures are random, so repeat until the result is statistically confident.
21	4. Name the culprit and pull the Entire checkpoint behind it, which holds the original request and the session.
22	5. Ask the owner one question (revert, or keep the intent and patch) and remember the ruling.
23	6. Fix, replay to prove the fix, add the case as a permanent regression test, and open a PR or an Entire Trail.
24	7. Write the damage (bad runs and dollars) to cfo.ai.
25	
26	Any description of the project opens with "which commit, and why". The fix comes after that.
27	
28	## Layout
29	
30	Python 3.12 through uv, in one repo.
31	
32	- `whodunit/case.py`: a case is a symptom, the failing inputs, a good ref, a bad ref and a check.
33	- `whodunit/suspects.py`: the commits in `good..bad` with their Entire checkpoint ids. Commits that cannot reach the agent's code get a lower prior (path filter first, then entire-graph impact).
34	- `whodunit/replay.py`: one git worktree per commit under test. It runs the target's replay command with the case input, tags the run with the commit SHA and case id, and reads the verdict from neatroots findings or a local check. A commit that will not build is skipped, like `git bisect skip`.
35	- `whodunit/lineup.py`: the statistical bisect, described below.
36	- `whodunit/motive.py`: `entire checkpoint explain` and `entire why` for the culprit, which give the original request and the session.
37	- `whodunit/brief.py`: the model writes the root-cause brief from the culprit diff, the relevant slice of the session transcript and a diff of a failing run against a passing one. Every sentence cites a span id, a commit or a checkpoint.
38	- `whodunit/ruling.py`: the ask-once memory (revert or patch, per kind of change), stored as files in the repo and mirrored to Entire Brain.
39	- `whodunit/fix.py`: applies the fix on a branch, replays the case until the posterior says it is fixed, adds the case to `cases/` as a regression test, and opens the PR or Trail.
40	- `whodunit/damages.py`: counts bad runs and cost from traces and writes them to cfo.ai.
41	- `whodunit/casefile/`: the static HTML case file, which is the main demo surface, and the CLI command `whodunit open-case`.
42	- `whodunit/onset.py`: reads the agent's ordinary runs from neatroots and brackets the failure between a good and a bad ref with the same change-point model. `--cloud` asks neatlogs when a detection began firing.
43	- `whodunit/neat.py`, `whodunit/llm.py`, `whodunit/env.py`: the MCP client for neatroots and neatlogs, the one place a model is asked for text, and the `.env` loader.
44	- `whodunit/simulate.py` and `whodunit/chart.py`: the simulator and its SVG charts. Results live in `eval/simulator/`.
45	- `whodunit/cli.py`: the commands. Each step reads and writes one case record, `<case>.record.json`, next to the case file.
46	- `eval/`: `score.py` scores cases against a sealed answer key, `traffic.py` sends everyday requests through a history, and `SECOND-SESSION.md` briefs the session that grows the victim.
47	- `tests/planted.py`: throwaway histories with a known culprit (an overpayment, a lookup that fails one run in three, a prompt change that needs a real model).
48	- `victims/refund-agent/`: the demo target. It starts from the refund agent in neatroots' `examples/` (Apache-2.0, and the README must say so) and grows to 40 or more commits through real coding-agent requests in a separate session, so the history and its checkpoints are genuine.
49	
50	### The statistical bisect
51	
52	Model a single change point c. The failure rate is p_good before c and p_bad from c onward. Estimate both rates by running the two endpoints several times and keeping Beta posteriors. Hold a posterior over c. Each round, replay the commit with the highest expected information gain and update with the Bernoulli outcome. The even split is kept as an option and does about as well. The prior on the good rate is about 5%, loosely held, which matters far more than the choice of picker. Stop at 95% on one commit or when the replay budget runs out, and in the second case report the remaining suspects with their probabilities.
53	
54	Unit-test it against a simulator. Publish the curve of accuracy against replay budget, next to plain bisect, at failure rates from 100% down to 20%.

1	"""The lineup: narrowing the suspects down to one commit.
2	
3	Plain bisect is right when the bug fails every time, and is the baseline. The statistical
4	bisect further down is for bugs that fail only some of the time.
5	"""
6	
7	import math
8	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
9	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
10	from typing import Callable, Sequence
11	
12	PASS, FAIL, SKIP = "pass", "fail", "skip"
13	
14	
15	@dataclass
16	class Lineup:
17	    culprit: int | None  # index into the suspects, or None if skips left more than one
18	    remaining: list[int]  # the suspects that could still be the first bad commit
19	    tested: list[tuple[int, str]] = field(default_factory=list)  # (index, verdict) in the order they ran
20	    posterior: list[float] | None = None  # P(first bad) per suspect, from the statistical bisect
21	    replays: int | None = None  # replays that returned a verdict
22	    rates: tuple[float, float] | None = None  # estimated failure rate before and from the top suspect
23	    note: str = ""  # why nobody was named, when the evidence itself was the problem
24	
25	
26	def plain_bisect(count: int, test: Callable[[int], str]) -> Lineup:
27	    """Find the first failing suspect among `count`, oldest first.
28	
29	    The commit before suspect 0 is known good and the last suspect is known bad. `test(i)` returns
30	    pass, fail or skip. A skipped commit cannot be judged, so the search steps to its nearest
31	    untested neighbour, as `git bisect skip` does. If only skipped commits separate the last
32	    pass from the first fail, they all stay in `remaining`.
33	    """
34	    if count < 1:
35	        raise ValueError("there are no suspects")
36	    good, bad = -1, count - 1  # the first bad commit is in (good, bad]
37	    skipped: set[int] = set()
38	    tested: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
39	    while True:
40	        open_ = [i for i in range(good + 1, bad) if i not in skipped]
41	        if not open_:
42	            break
43	        middle = (good + bad) / 2
44	        pick = min(open_, key=lambda i: (abs(i - middle), i))
45	        verdict = test(pick)
46	        tested.append((pick, verdict))
47	        if verdict == PASS:
48	            good = pick
49	        elif verdict == FAIL:
50	            bad = pick
51	        else:
52	            skipped.add(pick)
53	    remaining = list(range(good + 1, bad + 1))
54	    return Lineup(culprit=bad if len(remaining) == 1 else None, remaining=remaining, tested=tested)
55	
56	
57	def linear_scan_cost(culprit: int) -> int:
58	    """How many commits a scan from the oldest suspect tests before it meets the culprit."""
59	    return culprit + 1
60	
61	
62	
63	# The statistical bisect, for bugs that fail only some of the time.
64	#
65	# One change point c: every suspect before c fails at rate p_good, and c and everything after
66	# it fails at rate p_bad. Neither rate is known. Both get a Beta prior, and because a Beta prior
67	# with pass and fail counts integrates in closed form, the probability of the evidence under
68	# "c is the first bad commit" is exact. No sampling and no model.
69	
70	GOOD_PRIOR = (0.5, 9.5)  # Beta prior on the failure rate before the change: about 5%, loosely held
71	BAD_PRIOR = (1.0, 1.0)  # and from the change onward: anything from rare to always
72	
73	
74	def _log_beta(a: float, b: float) -> float:
75	    return math.lgamma(a) + math.lgamma(b) - math.lgamma(a + b)
76	
77	
78	def _entropy(q: float) -> float:
79	    return 0.0 if q <= 0.0 or q >= 1.0 else -(q * math.log(q) + (1.0 - q) * math.log(1.0 - q))
80	
81	
82	class ChangePoint:
83	    """What the replays so far say about which suspect is the first bad one.
84	
85	    Position -1 is the last good ref. Positions 0 to count-1 are the suspects, oldest first,
86	    and the last of them is the bad ref.
87	    """
88	
89	    def __init__(self, count: int, priors: Sequence[float] | None = None, good_prior=GOOD_PRIOR, bad_prior=BAD_PRIOR):
90	        self.good_prior, self.bad_prior = good_prior, bad_prior
91	        if count < 1:
92	            raise ValueError("there are no suspects")
93	        self.count = count
94	        weights = list(priors) if priors is not None else [1.0] * count
95	        if len(weights) != count or min(weights) < 0 or sum(weights) <= 0:
96	            raise ValueError("priors must be one weight per suspect, none negative")
97	        self.log_prior = [math.log(w) if w > 0 else -math.inf for w in weights]
98	        self.fails = [0] * (count + 1)  # slot 0 is the good ref
99	        self.passes = [0] * (count + 1)
100	
101	    def observe(self, position: int, failed: bool) -> None:
102	        (self.fails if failed else self.passes)[position + 1] += 1
103	
104	    @property
105	    def replays(self) -> int:
106	        return sum(self.fails) + sum(self.passes)
107	
108	    def _sides(self):
109	        """For each suspect c: fails and passes on the good side and on the bad side, if c is the first bad one."""
110	        total_f, total_p = sum(self.fails), sum(self.passes)
111	        good_f, good_p = self.fails[0], self.passes[0]
112	        for c in range(self.count):
113	            yield good_f, good_p, total_f - good_f, total_p - good_p
114	            good_f += self.fails[c + 1]
115	            good_p += self.passes[c + 1]
116	
117	    def posterior(self) -> list[float]:
118	        """P(suspect i is the first bad commit), for each suspect."""
119	        (ga, gb), (ba, bb) = self.good_prior, self.bad_prior
120	        logs = [
121	            self.log_prior[c] + _log_beta(ga + gf, gb + gp) + _log_beta(ba + bf, bb + bp)
122	            for c, (gf, gp, bf, bp) in enumerate(self._sides())
123	        ]
124	        top = max(logs)
125	        weights = [math.exp(v - top) for v in logs]
126	        norm = sum(weights)
127	        return [w / norm for w in weights]
128	
129	    def rates(self, culprit: int | None = None) -> list[tuple[float, float]] | tuple[float, float]:
130	        """Posterior mean failure rate (before, from) each suspect, or for one suspect."""
131	        (ga, gb), (ba, bb) = self.good_prior, self.bad_prior
132	        every = [((ga + gf) / (ga + gb + gf + gp), (ba + bf) / (ba + bb + bf + bp)) for gf, gp, bf, bp in self._sides()]
133	        return every if culprit is None else every[culprit]
134	
135	    def pick(self, posterior: Sequence[float], skipped: set[int] = frozenset(), how: str = "gain") -> int | None:
136	        """Which suspect to replay next. The last suspect is never picked, since it is bad either way.
137	
138	        "gain" picks the replay expected to tell us the most about which suspect is the first bad
139	        one (the mutual information between its outcome and c). "split" picks the suspect that
140	        divides the posterior mass most evenly, as plain bisect does. A pass at a commit that
141	        fails 30% of the time says little and a failure says a lot, which "gain" accounts for.
142	        In simulation the two end up close; see eval/simulator/README.md.
143	        """
144	        if how == "split":
145	            best, best_gap, mass = None, None, 0.0
146	            for i in range(self.count - 1):
147	                mass += posterior[i]
148	                if i in skipped:
149	                    continue
150	                gap = abs(mass - 0.5)
151	                if best_gap is None or gap < best_gap:
152	                    best, best_gap = i, gap
153	            return best
154	        rates = self.rates()
155	        # Replaying suspect i fails at the bad rate if c <= i and at the good rate if c > i.
156	        later_q = [0.0] * (self.count + 1)  # sum over c > i of P(c) * good rate
157	        later_h = [0.0] * (self.count + 1)
158	        for c in range(self.count - 1, -1, -1):
159	            later_q[c] = later_q[c + 1] + posterior[c] * rates[c][0]
160	            later_h[c] = later_h[c + 1] + posterior[c] * _entropy(rates[c][0])
161	        best, best_gain, q, h = None, -1.0, 0.0, 0.0
162	        for i in range(self.count - 1):
163	            q += posterior[i] * rates[i][1]
164	            h += posterior[i] * _entropy(rates[i][1])
165	            if i in skipped:
166	                continue
167	            gain = _entropy(q + later_q[i + 1]) - (h + later_h[i + 1])
168	            if gain > best_gain:
169	                best, best_gain = i, gain
170	        return best
171	
172	def statistical_bisect(
173	    count: int,
174	    trial: Callable[[int], str],
175	    budget: int,
176	    priors: Sequence[float] | None = None,
177	    confidence: float = 0.95,
178	    warmup: int = 6,
179	    parallel: int = 1,
180	    how: str = "gain",
181	    good_prior: tuple[float, float] = GOOD_PRIOR,
182	    bad_prior: tuple[float, float] = BAD_PRIOR,
183	    on_round: Callable[[list[int], list[str], list[float]], None] | None = None,
184	    evidence: Sequence[tuple[int, bool]] = (),
185	) -> Lineup:
186	    """Find the first bad suspect when a bad commit only fails some of the time.
187	
188	    `trial(position)` runs one replay and returns pass, fail or skip. Position -1 is the good
189	    ref. `budget` is the most replays to spend, counting the warm-up runs at both ends. Stops
190	    when one suspect holds `confidence` of the posterior, or when the budget is gone, in which
191	    case `remaining` lists the suspects still in play, most likely first.
192	
193	    `evidence` is what is already known, as (position, failed) pairs: replays from an earlier
194	    run of the same case, or the agent's ordinary traffic. It shapes the posterior from the
195	    start and does not count against the budget.
196	    """
197	    state = ChangePoint(count, priors, good_prior, bad_prior)
198	    for position, failed in evidence:
199	        state.observe(position, failed)
200	    known = state.replays
201	    tested: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
202	    skipped: set[int] = set()
203	    bad = count - 1
204	
205	    def run(positions: list[int]) -> list[str]:
206	        positions = positions[: max(0, budget - (state.replays - known))]
207	        if parallel > 1 and len(positions) > 1:
208	            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
209	                verdicts = list(pool.map(trial, positions))
210	        else:
211	            verdicts = [trial(p) for p in positions]
212	        for position, verdict in zip(positions, verdicts):
213	            tested.append((position, verdict))
214	            if verdict == SKIP:
215	                skipped.add(position)
216	            else:
217	                state.observe(position, verdict == FAIL)
218	        if on_round and positions:
219	            on_round(positions, verdicts, state.posterior())
220	        return verdicts
221	
222	    def finish(note: str = "") -> Lineup:
223	        posterior = state.posterior()
224	        ranked = sorted(range(count), key=lambda i: -posterior[i])
225	        top = ranked[0]
226	        named = top if posterior[top] >= confidence and not note else None
227	        remaining = [top] if named is not None else [i for i in ranked if posterior[i] >= 0.01]
228	        return Lineup(
229	            culprit=named, remaining=remaining, tested=tested, posterior=posterior,
230	            replays=state.replays, rates=state.rates(top), note=note,
231	        )
232	
233	    # Warm up at both ends, so the two failure rates start from evidence. Ends that earlier
234	    # evidence already covers need less of it.
235	    warmup = max(1, min(warmup, budget // 4))
236	    seen_good = state.fails[0] + state.passes[0]
237	    seen_bad = state.fails[bad + 1] + state.passes[bad + 1]
238	    first = []
239	    for n in range(warmup):
240	        if seen_good + n < warmup:
241	            first.append(-1)
242	        if seen_bad + n < warmup:
243	            first.append(bad)
244	    run(first)
245	    if -1 in skipped or bad in skipped:
246	        return finish("the good ref or the bad ref will not build")
247	    extra = 0
248	    while state.fails[bad + 1] == 0 and extra < 2 * warmup and state.replays - known < budget:
249	        run([bad] * max(1, parallel))  # a rare failure may simply not have shown yet
250	        extra += max(1, parallel)
251	    if state.fails[bad + 1] == 0:
252	        return finish(f"the bad ref passed all {state.passes[bad + 1]} of its replays")
253	
254	    while state.replays - known < budget:
255	        posterior = state.posterior()
256	        if max(posterior) >= confidence:
257	            break
258	        position = state.pick(posterior, skipped, how)
259	        if position is None:
260	            break
261	        run([position] * max(1, parallel))
262	    return finish()
263

1	"""The fix: apply it on a branch, replay the case until the evidence says it is fixed, and keep the case.
2	
3	A revert is mechanical. A patch that keeps the culprit's intent is written by a model and
4	checked the same way. Nothing here pushes or opens a pull request. That stays with the owner.
5	"""
6	
7	import math
8	import random
9	import re
10	import shutil
11	import subprocess
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	from . import llm
16	from .suspects import git
17	
18	
19	@dataclass
20	class Verification:
21	    fixed: bool
22	    probability: float  # P(its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit)
23	    replays: int
24	    failures: int
25	    note: str = ""
26	    better: float = 0.0  # P(it looks like the good side and not the bad side), the weaker claim
27	
28	
29	def _log_beta(a: float, b: float) -> float:
30	    return math.lgamma(a) + math.lgamma(b) - math.lgamma(a + b)
31	
32	
33	def probability_fixed(failures: int, passes: int, good: tuple[int, int], bad: tuple[int, int], prior: float = 0.5) -> float:
34	    """P(fixed) from replays of the fix commit, against what the lineup saw on each side.
35	
36	    `good` and `bad` are (failures, passes) from before the culprit and from it onward. Each
37	    side's failure rate is a Beta posterior, and the question is which side the fix commit's
38	    replays look like. This is the same closed form the lineup uses.
39	    """
40	    def evidence(side: tuple[int, int], a: float, b: float) -> float:
41	        a, b = a + side[0], b + side[1]
42	        return _log_beta(a + failures, b + passes) - _log_beta(a, b)
43	
44	    log_good = evidence(good, 0.5, 9.5) + math.log(prior)
45	    log_bad = evidence(bad, 1.0, 1.0) + math.log(1 - prior)
46	    top = max(log_good, log_bad)
47	    return math.exp(log_good - top) / (math.exp(log_good - top) + math.exp(log_bad - top))
48	
49	
50	def probability_back_to_baseline(failures: int, passes: int, good: tuple[int, int], margin: float = 0.05, samples: int = 20000) -> float:
51	    """P(the fix commit's failure rate is within `margin` of the rate before the culprit).
52	
53	    "Better than broken" is too low a bar: a patch that takes a bug from failing 9 runs in 10 to
54	    1 in 10 would pass it. This asks whether the failure rate is back where it was. Both rates
55	    are Beta posteriors and the comparison is done by sampling, with a fixed seed.
56	    """
57	    rng = random.Random(0)
58	    fa, fb = 0.5 + failures, 0.5 + passes
59	    ga, gb = 0.5 + good[0], 9.5 + good[1]
60	    hits = sum(rng.betavariate(fa, fb) <= rng.betavariate(ga, gb) + margin for _ in range(samples))
61	    return hits / samples
62	
63	
64	def verify(trial, good: tuple[int, int], bad: tuple[int, int], budget: int = 90, confidence: float = 0.95, parallel: int = 1, at_least: int = 12) -> Verification:
65	    """Replay the fix commit until its failure rate is 95% likely back to baseline, 95% likely not, or the budget is spent.
66	
67	    With a clean baseline that takes about 30 replays without a failure. `better` records the
68	    weaker claim, that the fix commit looks like the good side and not the bad side.
69	    """
70	    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
71	
72	    failures = passes = 0
73	    probability = 0.5
74	    while failures + passes < budget:
75	        batch = min(max(1, parallel), budget - failures - passes)
76	        if batch > 1:
77	            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=batch) as pool:
78	                verdicts = list(pool.map(lambda _: trial(), range(batch)))
79	        else:
80	            verdicts = [trial()]
81	        if "skip" in verdicts:
82	            return Verification(False, 0.0, failures + passes, failures, "the fix commit will not build")
83	        failures += verdicts.count("fail")
84	        passes += verdicts.count("pass")
85	        probability = probability_back_to_baseline(failures, passes, good)
86	        if failures + passes >= min(at_least, budget) and (probability >= confidence or probability <= 1 - confidence):
87	            break
88	    better = probability_fixed(failures, passes, good, bad)
89	    if probability >= confidence:
90	        note = ""
91	    elif probability <= 1 - confidence:
92	        note = "it still fails more often than before the culprit" + (", though less often than the broken commits do" if better >= confidence else "")
93	    else:
94	        note = "the replay budget ran out before the answer was clear"
95	    return Verification(probability >= confidence, probability, failures + passes, failures, note, better)
96	
97	
98	@dataclass
99	class Fix:
100	    branch: str
101	    kind: str  # revert or patch
102	    commit: str | None = None
103	    note: str = ""
104	    files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
105	
106	
107	def _commit(worktree: Path, message: str) -> str:
108	    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(worktree), "add", "-A"], check=True, capture_output=True)
109	    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(worktree), "commit", "-q", "-m", message], capture_output=True, text=True)
110	    if done.returncode != 0:
111	        raise RuntimeError(f"the fix could not be committed: {(done.stderr or done.stdout).strip()[:300]}")
112	    return git(worktree, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
113	
114	
115	def fix_worktree(repo: Path, branch: str, base: str) -> Path:
116	    """A worktree for the fix branch, starting from the bad ref."""
117	    path = repo / ".whodunit" / "fix" / branch.replace("/", "-")
118	    if path.exists():
119	        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path)], capture_output=True)
120	        shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)

127	def revert(repo: str | Path, culprit: str, base: str, case_id: str) -> Fix:
128	    """Revert the culprit on a new branch that starts at the bad ref."""
129	    repo = Path(repo).resolve()
130	    branch = f"whodunit/{case_id}"
131	    worktree = fix_worktree(repo, branch, base)
132	    subject = git(repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%s", culprit).strip()
133	    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(worktree), "revert", "--no-commit", culprit], capture_output=True, text=True)
134	    note = ""
135	    if done.returncode != 0:
136	        clashing = [f for f in git(worktree, "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=U").split("\n") if f]
137	        if clashing and all(f.lower().endswith((".md", ".txt", ".rst")) for f in clashing):
138	            # The clash is in documents the agent does not run. Keep them as they are and revert the rest.
139	            for name in clashing:
140	                subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(worktree), "checkout", "--ours", "--", name], capture_output=True)
141	                subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(worktree), "add", "--", name], capture_output=True)
142	            note = f"The revert clashed with later edits to {', '.join(clashing)}, which the agent does not run, so those were left as they are."
143	        else:
144	            said = (done.stdout + "\n" + done.stderr).splitlines()
145	            why = next((line.strip() for line in said if line.startswith(("CONFLICT", "error:"))), "git gave no detail")
146	            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(worktree), "revert", "--abort"], capture_output=True)
147	            return Fix(branch, "revert", note="The revert does not apply cleanly on top of the later commits. " + why)
148	    files = [f for f in git(worktree, "diff", "--cached", "--name-only").split("\n") if f]
149	    sha = _commit(worktree, f"Revert \"{subject}\"\n\nWhodunit case {case_id} named {culprit[:12]} as the commit that broke the agent.")
150	    return Fix(branch, "revert", sha, note=note, files=files)

152	
153	PATCH_SYSTEM = """You fix a regression in an AI agent without undoing what the change was for.
154	You get the request behind the culprit commit, its diff, the root-cause brief and the current content of each file it touched.
155	Keep the intent of the request. Remove only the behaviour that causes the failure. Change as little as you can.
156	Answer with edits and nothing else, in this form, one block per place you change:
157	
158	=== path/to/file
159	<<<<<<< SEARCH
160	lines exactly as they are in the file now, enough of them to be unique
161	=======
162	the lines that replace them
163	>>>>>>> REPLACE
164	=== end"""
165	
166	EDIT = re.compile(r"<<<<<<< SEARCH\n(.*?)\n=======\n(.*?)\n?>>>>>>> REPLACE", re.S)
167	
168	
169	def apply_edits(answer: str, worktree: Path, allowed: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
170	    """Apply the model's edits. Returns (files changed, what went wrong, if anything)."""
171	    changed, problems = [], []
172	    for block in answer.split("\n=== end"):
173	        head, _, body = block.partition("=== ")[2].partition("\n")
174	        name = head.strip()
175	        if not name:
176	            continue
177	        if name not in allowed:
178	            problems.append(f"{name} is not one of the files the culprit touched")
179	            continue
180	        text = original = (worktree / name).read_text()
181	        edits = EDIT.findall(body)
182	        if not edits and body.strip() and "<<<<<<<" not in body:
183	            text = body.rstrip("\n") + "\n"  # a whole file, which is also accepted
184	        for search, replace in edits:
185	            if text.count(search) != 1:
186	                problems.append(f"an edit to {name} matched {text.count(search)} places and needs to match exactly one")
187	                continue
188	            text = text.replace(search, replace)
189	        if text != original:
190	            (worktree / name).write_text(text)
191	            changed.append(name)
192	    return changed, "; ".join(problems)
193	
194	
195	def patch(repo: str | Path, culprit: str, base: str, case_id: str, target: str, request: str | None, brief: dict | None, feedback: str = "") -> Fix:
196	    """Ask a model for a patch that keeps the culprit's intent, and commit it on a new branch."""
197	    repo = Path(repo).resolve()
198	    branch = f"whodunit/{case_id}"
199	    worktree = fix_worktree(repo, branch, base)
200	    subject = git(repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%s", culprit).strip()
201	    files = [f for f in git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", culprit, "--", target).split("\n") if f and (worktree / f).is_file()]
202	    if not files:
203	        return Fix(branch, "patch", note="None of the files the culprit touched exist at the bad ref.")
204	    parts = [
205	        f"Request behind the culprit commit: {request or 'not recorded'}",
206	        f"Culprit commit {culprit[:12]}: {subject}",
207	        "Its diff:\n" + git(repo, "show", "--format=", culprit, "--", target)[:6000],
208	        "Root-cause brief:\n" + "\n".join(s["text"] for s in (brief or {}).get("sentences", [])),
209	    ]
210	    if feedback:
211	        parts.append("An earlier patch was tried and the failure is still there. What happened:\n" + feedback)
212	    parts += [f"Current content of {f}:\n{(worktree / f).read_text()}" for f in files]
213	    try:
214	        answer = llm.ask(PATCH_SYSTEM, "\n\n".join(parts), max_tokens=3000, timeout=300)
215	    except llm.LlmError as exc:
216	        return Fix(branch, "patch", note=f"No patch was written: {exc}")
217	    changed, problems = apply_edits(answer, worktree, files)
218	    if not changed or not git(worktree, "status", "--porcelain").strip():
219	        return Fix(branch, "patch", note="The model's answer changed none of the culprit's files." + (f" {problems}." if problems else ""))
220	    sha = _commit(worktree, f"Patch the regression from \"{subject}\"\n\nWhodunit case {case_id} named {culprit[:12]}. This keeps what that commit was for and removes the failure.")
221	    return Fix(branch, "patch", sha, files=changed)

74	    def on_round(positions: list[int], verdicts: list[str], posterior: list[float]) -> None:
75	        top = max(range(len(posterior)), key=posterior.__getitem__)
76	        for position in dict.fromkeys(positions):
77	            who = "last good " if position < 0 else f"suspect {position + 1:>2}"
78	            marks = "".join("F" if v == FAIL else "." if v == PASS else "s" for p, v in zip(positions, verdicts) if p == position)
79	            say(f"  {who}  {marks:<8}  top suspect {top + 1:>2} at {posterior[top]:5.1%}")

303	def _sides(record: dict) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]:
304	    """(failures, passes) the lineup saw before the culprit, and from it onward."""
305	    order = {s["sha"]: n for n, s in enumerate(record["suspects"])}
306	    at = order[record["lineup"]["culprit"]["sha"]]
307	    good, bad = [0, 0], [0, 0]
308	    for replay in record.get("replays", []):
309	        if replay["verdict"] in ("pass", "fail"):
310	            side = bad if order.get(replay["sha"], -1) >= at else good
311	            side[0 if replay["verdict"] == "fail" else 1] += 1
312	    return tuple(good), tuple(bad)

315	def _attempt(kind: str, case, repo: Path, record: dict, args, feedback: str = "") -> dict:
316	    """Make one fix and replay it. Returns what was tried and how it went."""
317	    culprit = record["lineup"]["culprit"]["sha"]
318	    if kind == rulings.REVERT:
319	        made = fixes.revert(repo, culprit, record["case"]["bad"], case.id)
320	    else:
321	        made = fixes.patch(repo, culprit, record["case"]["bad"], case.id, case.target, (record.get("motive") or {}).get("request"), record.get("brief"), feedback)
322	    attempt = asdict(made)
323	    if made.commit is None:
324	        print(f"  {kind}: no fix was made. {made.note}")
325	        return attempt
326	    print(f"  {kind}: committed as {made.commit[:12]} on branch {made.branch}. Replaying to check it.")
327	    good, bad = _sides(record)
328	    with Runner(repo, case, keep=getattr(args, "keep", False)) as runner:
329	        checked = fixes.verify(lambda: runner.trial(made.commit), good, bad, budget=args.fix_budget, parallel=args.parallel)
330	        attempt["failed_replays"] = [f"{r.input} -> {r.reason}" for r in runner.replays if r.verdict == FAIL][:4]
331	    attempt["verification"] = asdict(checked)
332	    attempt["diff"] = git(repo, "show", "--format=", made.commit)[:4000]
333	    print(f"  {kind}: {checked.failures} failures in {checked.replays} replays. Probability the failure rate is back to where it was: {checked.probability:.1%}." + (f" Not proven: {checked.note}." if checked.note else ""))
334	    return attempt

341	def fix(args) -> int:
342	    """Apply the ruling on a branch and replay until the evidence says fixed. If it is not, try again.
343	
344	    A patch that is not proven gets one more try, with the first patch and its failing replays
345	    in front of the model. If that is not proven either, the culprit is reverted, which is the
346	    safe answer and loses what the commit was for. Every try is kept in the record.
347	    """
348	    loaded = _need_culprit(args)
349	    if loaded is None:
350	        return 2
351	    case, repo, record, path = loaded
352	    if not record.get("ruling"):
353	        print(f"No ruling yet. Run `whodunit ruling {args.case}` first.")
354	        return 2
355	    wanted = record["ruling"]["ruling"]
356	    attempts = [_attempt(wanted, case, repo, record, args)]
357	    if wanted == rulings.PATCH and not _proven(attempts[-1]):
358	        first = attempts[-1]
359	        feedback = (first.get("note") or "") + "\nThe first patch:\n" + first.get("diff", "none was made") + "\nReplays of it that still failed:\n" + "\n".join(first.get("failed_replays", []) or ["none recorded"])
360	        print("  The patch is not proven. Trying once more, with the first patch and its failures in view.")
361	        attempts.append(_attempt(rulings.PATCH, case, repo, record, args, feedback))
362	    if wanted == rulings.PATCH and not _proven(attempts[-1]):
363	        print("  Still not proven. Falling back to a revert, which loses what the commit was for.")
364	        attempts.append(_attempt(rulings.REVERT, case, repo, record, args))
365	        attempts[-1]["note"] = ((attempts[-1].get("note") or "") + " This is a fallback: the ruling was to patch, and two patches were not proven.").strip()
366	    final = next((a for a in reversed(attempts) if _proven(a)), attempts[-1])
367	    record["fix"] = final
368	    record["attempts"] = attempts
369	    if _proven(final):
370	        kept = Path.cwd() / "cases" / f"{case.id}.toml"
371	        kept.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
372	        text = Path(args.case).read_text().rstrip("\n")
373	        if "\nfixed = " in "\n" + text:
374	            text = "\n".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith(("fixed = ", "# Closed by Whodunit")))
375	        # Top-level keys have to come before the first table in TOML, so the line goes at the top.
376	        text = f'# Closed by Whodunit. Replay with `whodunit check cases/{case.id}.toml`.\nfixed = "{final["commit"]}"\n' + text
377	        kept.write_text(text + "\n")
378	        record["fix"]["regression_case"] = os.path.relpath(kept)
379	    save_record(path, record)
380	    if _proven(final):
381	        print(f"Fixed by {final['kind']} {final['commit'][:12]} after {len(attempts)} {'try' if len(attempts) == 1 else 'tries'}. Kept as a regression test: {record['fix']['regression_case']}")
382	        print(f"The branch {final['branch']} is local. Pushing it and opening a pull request is the owner's call.")
383	    else:
384	        print(f"Not fixed after {len(attempts)} {'try' if len(attempts) == 1 else 'tries'}. The record has each one.")
385	    return 0 if _proven(final) else 1

556	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
557	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="whodunit", description="Find the commit that broke an AI agent.")
558	    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
559	    p = commands.add_parser("lineup", help="replay a case against the suspect commits and name the culprit")
560	    p.add_argument("case", help="path to a case file (TOML)")
561	    p.add_argument("--repo", default=".", help="the git repo that holds the agent (default: here)")
562	    p.add_argument("--method", choices=("statistical", "plain"), default="statistical", help="plain is for bugs that fail every time")
563	    p.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=1, help="with --method plain, how many times a commit must pass all inputs to be called good")
564	    p.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=120, help="most replays the statistical bisect may spend (default 120)")
565	    p.add_argument("--confidence", type=float, default=0.95, help="posterior needed to name a culprit (default 0.95)")
566	    p.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=1, help="replays to run at once")
567	    p.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true", help="start from the replays already in the case record; --budget is then how many more to spend")
568	    p.add_argument("--from-traffic", metavar="WORKFLOW", help="start from ordinary runs of this workflow that already asked what the case asks")
569	    p.add_argument("--no-graph", action="store_true", help="do not ask entire-graph which commits could reach the agent")
570	    p.add_argument("--no-priors", action="store_true", help="suspect every commit equally, even ones that never touched the agent")
571	    p.add_argument("--record", help="where to write the case record (default: next to the case file)")
572	    p.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true", help="leave the worktrees in .whodunit/worktrees")
573	    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print the result as JSON on stdout")
574	    p.set_defaults(func=lineup)
575	    for name, func, text in (
576	        ("brief", brief, "write the root-cause brief for a case that has a culprit"),
577	        ("ruling", ruling, "ask the owner once per kind of change: revert, or keep the intent and patch"),
578	        ("fix", fix, "apply the ruling on a branch and replay until the fix is proven"),
579	        ("damages", damages, "count the bad runs and what they cost"),
580	    ):
581	        p = commands.add_parser(name, help=text)
582	        p.add_argument("case", help="path to the case file")
583	        p.add_argument("--record", help="the case record (default: next to the case file)")
584	        p.set_defaults(func=func)
585	        if name == "brief":
586	            p.add_argument("--no-runs", action="store_true", help="do not ask neatroots for a failing and a passing run")
587	        if name == "ruling":
588	            p.add_argument("--answer", choices=("revert", "patch"), help="give the ruling here instead of being asked")
589	        if name == "fix":
590	            p.add_argument("--fix-budget", type=int, default=90, help="most replays to spend checking one fix")
591	            p.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=1)
592	            p.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true")
593	        if name == "damages":
594	            p.add_argument("--workflow", default="refund-agent")
595	            p.add_argument("--since-ms", type=float, help="count runs from this time, in ms since the epoch")
596	    p = commands.add_parser("investigate", help="run a whole case from lineup to case file, stopping only for the owner's ruling")
597	    p.add_argument("case", help="path to the case file")
598	    p.add_argument("--repo", default=".")
599	    p.add_argument("--record")
600	    p.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=120, help="replays the lineup may spend before it stops to think again")
601	    p.add_argument("--fix-budget", type=int, default=90, help="most replays to spend checking one fix")
602	    p.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=3)
603	    p.add_argument("--answer", choices=("revert", "patch"), help="the owner's ruling, if there is no standing rule yet")
604	    p.add_argument("--workflow", default="refund-agent")
605	    p.add_argument("--redo-brief", action="store_true")
606	    p.add_argument("--fresh", action="store_true", help="set aside any earlier record for this case and start over")
607	    p.add_argument("--from-traffic", metavar="WORKFLOW", help="start the lineup from ordinary runs of this workflow")
608	    p.add_argument("--no-graph", action="store_true")
609	    p.set_defaults(func=investigate)
610	    p = commands.add_parser("casebook", help="write every case file in a folder and an index page")
611	    p.add_argument("folder", nargs="?", default="cases")
612	    p.add_argument("--open", action="store_true")
613	    p.set_defaults(func=casebook)
614	    p = commands.add_parser("onset", help="find when the failures began and between which commits, from ordinary runs")
615	    p.add_argument("--workflow", default="refund-agent")
616	    p.add_argument("--cloud", metavar="DETECTION", help="also ask neatlogs cloud when this detection started firing")
617	    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
618	    p.set_defaults(func=onset)
619	    p = commands.add_parser("open-case", help="write the case file page and open it")
620	    p.add_argument("case")
621	    p.add_argument("--record")
622	    p.add_argument("--no-open", action="store_true", help="write the page without opening a browser")
623	    p.set_defaults(func=open_case)
624	    p = commands.add_parser("check", help="replay a kept case against a ref, as a regression test")
625	    p.add_argument("case")
626	    p.add_argument("--repo", default=".")
627	    p.add_argument("--ref", help="the commit to replay against (default: the case's fix, or HEAD if it has none)")
628	    p.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=6)
629	    p.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=3)
630	    p.add_argument("--record")
631	    p.set_defaults(func=check)
632	    p = commands.add_parser("motive", help="show what a commit was asked to do, from its Entire checkpoint")

1	"""Replay a case's inputs against a commit, in a git worktree of its own."""
2	
3	import hashlib
4	import os
5	import signal
6	import subprocess
7	import threading
8	import time
9	from collections import defaultdict
10	from dataclasses import dataclass
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from .case import Case, CaseInput, judge
14	from .suspects import git, resolve
15	
16	PASS, FAIL, SKIP = "pass", "fail", "skip"
17	
18	
19	@dataclass(frozen=True)
20	class Replay:
21	    sha: str
22	    input: str
23	    verdict: str  # pass, fail or skip
24	    reason: str
25	    seconds: float
26	    started: float = 0.0  # wall clock, seconds since the epoch
27	    tag: str = ""  # the case tag this replay's run carries in its trace, unique to the replay
28	
29	
30	def run_command(command: list[str], cwd: Path, env: dict, timeout: float) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
31	    """Like subprocess.run, but a timeout stops the whole process group.
32	
33	    The replay command is usually `uv run ...`, which starts the agent as a child. Killing only
34	    `uv` would leave the agent running.
35	    """
36	    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, start_new_session=True)
37	    try:
38	        stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
39	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
40	        try:
41	            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
42	        except ProcessLookupError:
43	            pass
44	        process.communicate()
45	        raise
46	    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)
47	
48	
49	class Runner:
50	    """Keeps one worktree per commit under .whodunit/worktrees and counts every replay it runs."""
51	
52	    def __init__(self, repo: str | Path, case: Case, keep: bool = False):
53	        self.repo = Path(repo).resolve()
54	        self.case = case
55	        self.keep = keep
56	        # One folder per runner, so two runs in the same repo never remove each other's worktrees.
57	        self.root = self.repo / ".whodunit" / "worktrees" / str(os.getpid())
58	        self.built: dict[str, str | None] = {}  # sha -> None if the build worked, else why it did not
59	        self.replays: list[Replay] = []
60	        self._locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = defaultdict(threading.Lock)  # one build at a time per commit
61	        self._turn: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)  # which input a commit gets next
62	        self._count = 0
63	        self._first = int(time.time()) % 100000 * 1000  # so tags from separate runs of one case never collide
64	        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.repo), "worktree", "prune"], capture_output=True)
65	
66	    def __enter__(self):
67	        return self
68	
69	    def __exit__(self, *exc):
70	        if not self.keep:
71	            self.clean()
72	
73	    def worktree(self, sha: str) -> Path:
74	        path = self.root / sha[:12]
75	        if not path.exists():
76	            self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
77	            git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--force", str(path), sha)
78	        return path
79	
80	    def clean(self) -> None:
81	        for sha in list(self.built):
82	            path = self.root / sha[:12]
83	            if path.exists():
84	                subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path)], capture_output=True)
85	        self.built.clear()
86	        try:
87	            self.root.rmdir()
88	        except OSError:
89	            pass
90	
91	    def _env(self, sha: str, tag: str = "") -> dict:
92	        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "VIRTUAL_ENV"}
93	        env.update(self.case.env)
94	        env["WHODUNIT_COMMIT"] = sha
95	        if self.case.id:
96	            env["WHODUNIT_CASE"] = tag or self.case.id
97	        else:
98	            env.pop("WHODUNIT_CASE", None)  # ordinary traffic carries no case tag
99	        lock = self.root / sha[:12] / self.case.target / "uv.lock"
100	        if lock.is_file():
101	            # Worktrees with the same lockfile share one environment, so a new commit does not
102	            # mean a new install. A commit that changes the lockfile gets its own.
103	            digest = hashlib.sha256(lock.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]
104	            env.setdefault("UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT", str(self.repo / ".whodunit" / "envs" / digest))
105	        dotenv = self.repo / ".env"
106	        if dotenv.is_file():
107	            env.setdefault("WHODUNIT_ENV", str(dotenv))  # a path only; the agent reads the keys itself
108	        return env
109	
110	    def build(self, sha: str) -> str | None:
111	        """Check the commit out and build it once. Returns why it failed, or None."""
112	        with self._locks[sha]:
113	            return self._build(sha)
114	
115	    def _build(self, sha: str) -> str | None:
116	        if sha in self.built:
117	            return self.built[sha]
118	        problem = None
119	        cwd = self.worktree(sha) / self.case.target
120	        if not cwd.is_dir():
121	            problem = f"{self.case.target} does not exist at this commit"
122	        elif self.case.build:
123	            try:
124	                done = run_command(list(self.case.build), cwd, self._env(sha), self.case.timeout)
125	                if done.returncode != 0:
126	                    problem = "build failed: " + ((done.stderr.strip() or done.stdout.strip()).splitlines() or ["no output"])[-1]
127	            except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
128	                problem = f"build failed: {exc}"
129	        self.built[sha] = problem
130	        return problem
131	
132	    def replay(self, ref: str, case_input: CaseInput) -> Replay:
133	        """Run the agent once at this commit with this input and judge the result."""
134	        sha = resolve(self.repo, ref)
135	        started, clock = time.monotonic(), time.time()
136	        with self._locks["#"]:
137	            self._count += 1
138	            # The agent writes WHODUNIT_CASE into its trace, so a number after the case id lets
139	            # one replay be matched to exactly one run afterwards.
140	            tag = f"{self.case.id}/{self._first + self._count}" if self.case.id else ""
141	        problem = self.build(sha)
142	        if problem:
143	            verdict, reason = SKIP, problem
144	        else:
145	            cwd = self.worktree(sha) / self.case.target
146	            command = [part.replace("{input}", case_input.text) for part in self.case.run]
147	            try:
148	                done = run_command(command, cwd, self._env(sha, tag), self.case.timeout)
149	                passed, reason = judge(self.case, case_input, done.stdout, cwd)
150	                if not passed and done.returncode != 0:
151	                    reason = f"exit {done.returncode}: " + ((done.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [reason])[-1])
152	                verdict = PASS if passed else FAIL
153	            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
154	                verdict, reason = FAIL, f"timed out after {self.case.timeout:.0f}s"
155	        result = Replay(sha=sha, input=case_input.text, verdict=verdict, reason=reason, seconds=time.monotonic() - started, started=clock, tag=tag)
156	        self.replays.append(result)
157	        return result
158	
159	    def test_commit(self, ref: str) -> tuple[str, list[Replay]]:
160	        """Every input once. The commit fails if any input fails, and is skipped if it will not build."""
161	        results = []
162	        for case_input in self.case.inputs:
163	            result = self.replay(ref, case_input)
164	            results.append(result)
165	            if result.verdict != PASS:
166	                return result.verdict, results
167	        return PASS, results
168	
169	    def trial(self, ref: str) -> str:
170	        """One replay at this commit, taking the case inputs in turn. This is what the statistical bisect calls."""
171	        sha = resolve(self.repo, ref)
172	        with self._locks[sha]:
173	            turn = self._turn[sha]
174	            self._turn[sha] += 1
175	        return self.replay(sha, self.case.inputs[turn % len(self.case.inputs)]).verdict

1	"""Alibis from entire-graph: can this commit's changes reach the agent at all?
2	
3	`entire graph commit` lists what a commit changed as entities (a function, a module body, a
4	document) and `entire graph impact` gives a symbol's callers. A commit that only touched the
5	README, or a helper script the agent never calls, has an alibi and starts with less suspicion.
6	It is never cleared outright: the lineup can still land on it if the replays say so.
7	"""
8	
9	import json
10	import subprocess
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from .suspects import git
14	
15	REACHES, UNKNOWN, DATA, UNCALLED, DOCS, ELSEWHERE = 1.0, 1.0, 0.6, 0.15, 0.05, 0.05
16	DOC_LANGUAGES = {"Markdown", "Git Ignore", "Text", "HTML", "CSS"}
17	CODE_LANGUAGES = {"Python", "TypeScript", "JavaScript", "Go", "Rust", "Java", "Ruby"}
18	
19	
20	def _graph(repo: str | Path, *args: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict | None:
21	    """Run an entire-graph command that prints JSON. None if the plugin is missing or the call fails."""
22	    try:
23	        done = subprocess.run(["entire", "graph", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
24	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
25	        return None
26	    if done.returncode != 0:
27	        return None
28	    try:
29	        return json.loads(done.stdout)
30	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
31	        return None
32	
33	
34	def changes(repo: str | Path, sha: str) -> list[dict] | None:
35	    """What a commit changed, one entry per entity: {"path", "language", "kind", "name", "type", "dependents"}."""
36	    found = _graph(repo, "commit", sha, "--json")
37	    if found is None:
38	        return None
39	    out = []
40	    for file in found.get("files") or []:
41	        listed = file.get("changes") or [{"kind": "file", "name": file["path"], "type": file.get("status", "M")}]
42	        for change in listed:
43	            out.append({
44	                "path": file["path"], "language": file.get("language") or "", "kind": change.get("kind", ""),
45	                "name": change.get("name", ""), "type": change.get("type", ""), "dependents": change.get("dependents_count", 0),
46	            })
47	    return out
48	
49	
50	def called_from(repo: str | Path, name: str, path: str, entry: str) -> bool | None:
51	    """Is this symbol called, directly or through one other function, by code in the entry file? None if unknown."""
52	    found = _graph(repo, "impact", "--symbol", name, "--file", path, "--repo", ".", "--depth", "2", "--limit", "60", "--format", "json", "--head")
53	    if found is None or not found.get("focus") or found.get("disambiguation_required"):
54	        return None
55	    callers = [entry_["endpoint"].get("file_path", "") for entry_ in (found.get("callers") or {}).get("entries", [])]
56	    return entry in callers
57	
58	
59	def alibi(repo: str | Path, sha: str, target: str, entry: str = "agent.py") -> tuple[float, str]:
60	    """(prior weight, reason) for one suspect. A weight of 1 means no alibi."""
61	    prefix = "" if target in (".", "") else target.rstrip("/") + "/"
62	    entry_path = prefix + entry
63	    listed = changes(repo, sha)
64	    if listed is None:
65	        return UNKNOWN, "entire-graph could not read this commit"
66	    # Files the graph does not parse (a lockfile, say) are missing from its list. Git knows them.
67	    seen = {c["path"] for c in listed}
68	    for path in git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-m", "--first-parent", sha).split("\n"):
69	        if path and path not in seen:
70	            listed.append({"path": path, "language": "Markdown" if path.endswith((".md", ".txt")) else "", "kind": "file", "name": path, "type": "M", "dependents": 0})
71	    inside = [c for c in listed if c["path"].startswith(prefix)]
72	    if not inside:
73	        return ELSEWHERE, "never touched the agent's folder"
74	    best, why = 0.0, ""
75	    for change in inside:
76	        short = change["path"][len(prefix):]
77	        if change["language"] in DOC_LANGUAGES:
78	            weight, reason = DOCS, f"only touched {short}, which the agent does not run"
79	        elif change["language"] not in CODE_LANGUAGES:
80	            weight, reason = DATA, f"changed {short}, a data or dependency file the graph cannot follow"
81	        elif change["path"] == entry_path:
82	            weight, reason = REACHES, f"changed {change['name'] if change['kind'] != 'module' else 'the body of ' + short}, in the agent's own file"
83	        elif change["kind"] in ("module", "file"):
84	            weight, reason = UNCALLED, f"changed {short}, a separate script"
85	        else:
86	            reached = called_from(repo, change["name"], change["path"], entry_path)
87	            if reached is None:
88	                weight, reason = UNKNOWN, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, and the graph has no record of its callers"
89	            elif reached:
90	                weight, reason = REACHES, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, which the agent calls"
91	            else:
92	                weight, reason = UNCALLED, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, which the agent never calls"
93	        if weight > best:
94	            best, why = weight, reason
95	    return best, why

1	"""The suspects: every commit after the last good ref, up to and including the first bad one."""
2	
3	import subprocess
4	from dataclasses import dataclass
5	from pathlib import Path
6	
7	# A commit that never touched the agent's folder can still be guilty (a shared file, a
8	# lockfile higher up), so it keeps a small prior. Plain bisect ignores priors.
9	PRIOR_TOUCHES_TARGET = 1.0
10	PRIOR_ELSEWHERE = 0.05
11	
12	
13	@dataclass(frozen=True)
14	class Suspect:
15	    sha: str
16	    subject: str
17	    files: tuple[str, ...]
18	    checkpoint: str | None  # Entire checkpoint id from the commit trailer
19	    touches_target: bool
20	    prior: float
21	    alibi: str = ""  # why this commit starts with less suspicion, when entire-graph gives a reason
22	
23	    @property
24	    def short(self) -> str:
25	        return self.sha[:12]
26	
27	
28	def git(repo: str | Path, *args: str) -> str:
29	    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
30	    if done.returncode != 0:
31	        raise RuntimeError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed: {done.stderr.strip()}")
32	    return done.stdout
33	
34	
35	def resolve(repo: str | Path, ref: str) -> str:
36	    return git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{ref}^{{commit}}").strip()
37	
38	
39	def list_suspects(repo: str | Path, good: str, bad: str, target: str = ".", graph: bool = False) -> list[Suspect]:
40	    """Commits in good..bad, oldest first. The last one is the bad ref itself.
41	
42	    The path filter gives the first prior: a commit that never touched the agent's folder keeps
43	    a small one. With `graph`, entire-graph refines it for the commits that did, by asking
44	    whether what they changed is something the agent runs.
45	    """
46	    shas = git(repo, "rev-list", "--reverse", "--ancestry-path", f"{good}..{bad}").split()
47	    prefix = "" if target in (".", "") else target.rstrip("/") + "/"
48	    suspects = []
49	    for sha in shas:
50	        subject, _, trailer = git(
51	            repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%s%x00%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly,separator=%x20)", sha
52	        ).strip().partition("\x00")
53	        files = tuple(git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-m", "--first-parent", sha).split("\n"))
54	        files = tuple(f for f in files if f)
55	        touches = any(f.startswith(prefix) for f in files)
56	        prior, alibi = (PRIOR_TOUCHES_TARGET, "") if touches else (PRIOR_ELSEWHERE, "never touched the agent's folder")
57	        if graph and touches:
58	            from .graph import alibi as graph_alibi  # imported here because graph.py uses git() from this module
59	
60	            prior, reason = graph_alibi(repo, sha, target)
61	            alibi = reason if prior < 1.0 else ""
62	        suspects.append(Suspect(
63	            sha=sha, subject=subject, files=files, checkpoint=trailer.split()[0] if trailer.strip() else None,
64	            touches_target=touches, prior=prior, alibi=alibi,
65	        ))
66	    return suspects

1	"""The motive: what was the culprit commit asked to do?
2	
3	Entire keeps a checkpoint for a commit that followed coding-agent work, with the session
4	transcript behind it. This module finds the request that led to the commit and the part of
5	the session where the agent worked on it.
6	"""
7	
8	import json
9	import re
10	import subprocess
11	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
12	from datetime import datetime, timezone
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	from .suspects import git
16	
17	MAX_TEXT = 1200  # characters kept from any one transcript entry
18	
19	
20	@dataclass
21	class Step:
22	    """One thing the coding agent said or did between the request and the commit."""
23	
24	    id: str  # transcript entry id, shortened, so a brief can cite it
25	    kind: str  # said, edited, ran or read
26	    text: str
27	    file: str | None = None
28	
29	
30	@dataclass
31	class Motive:
32	    sha: str
33	    subject: str
34	    checkpoint: str | None = None
35	    session: str | None = None
36	    agent: str | None = None
37	    model: str | None = None
38	    request: str | None = None  # the prompt that led to the commit
39	    message: str = ""  # the commit message body, which is all there is when no session can be read
40	    request_id: str | None = None
41	    request_time: str | None = None
42	    earlier_requests: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # prompts before it in the same session, oldest first
43	    steps: list[Step] = field(default_factory=list)
44	    link: str | None = None
45	    note: str = ""  # why something is missing
46	
47	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
48	        return asdict(self)
49	
50	
51	def entire(repo: str | Path, *args: str) -> str | None:
52	    """Run the Entire CLI. Returns None if it is not installed or the call fails."""
53	    try:
54	        done = subprocess.run(["entire", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
55	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
56	        return None
57	    return done.stdout if done.returncode == 0 else None
