59	
60	def checkpoint_link(repo: str | Path, sha: str) -> str | None:
61	    """https://entire.io/gh/OWNER/REPO/commit/FULL_SHA, if the repo has a GitHub remote."""
62	    try:
63	        url = git(repo, "remote", "get-url", "origin").strip()
64	    except RuntimeError:
65	        return None
66	    match = re.search(r"github\.com[:/]([^/]+)/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$", url)
67	    return f"https://entire.io/gh/{match.group(1)}/{match.group(2)}/commit/{sha}" if match else None
68	
69	
70	def _when(stamp: str | None) -> datetime | None:
71	    if not stamp:
72	        return None
73	    try:
74	        return datetime.fromisoformat(stamp.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
75	    except ValueError:
76	        return None
77	
78	
79	def _prompt_text(entry: dict) -> str | None:
80	    """The text of a prompt a person typed, or None for tool results and injected context."""
81	    if entry.get("type") != "user" or entry.get("isMeta") or entry.get("isSidechain"):
82	        return None
83	    content = entry.get("message", {}).get("content")
84	    if isinstance(content, str):
85	        return content.strip() or None
86	    if isinstance(content, list) and not any(b.get("type") == "tool_result" for b in content):
87	        text = "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text").strip()
88	        return text or None
89	    return None
90	
91	
92	def _steps(entry: dict, files: set[str]) -> list[Step]:
93	    """What an assistant entry said and did. Edits and reads are kept only for files in the commit."""
94	    out = []
95	    entry_id = (entry.get("uuid") or "")[:8]
96	    for block in entry.get("message", {}).get("content", []) or []:
97	        if block.get("type") == "text" and block.get("text", "").strip():
98	            out.append(Step(entry_id, "said", block["text"].strip()[:MAX_TEXT]))
99	        elif block.get("type") == "tool_use":
100	            name, given = block.get("name", ""), block.get("input", {}) or {}
101	            path = given.get("file_path") or ""
102	            touched = next((f for f in files if path.endswith(f)), None)
103	            if name in ("Edit", "Write", "NotebookEdit") and touched:
104	                change = given.get("new_string") or given.get("content") or ""
105	                out.append(Step(entry_id, "edited", change[:MAX_TEXT], touched))
106	            elif name == "Read" and touched:
107	                out.append(Step(entry_id, "read", touched, touched))
108	            elif name == "Bash" and (given.get("description") or given.get("command")):
109	                out.append(Step(entry_id, "ran", (given.get("description") or given["command"])[:300]))
110	    return out
111	
112	
113	def read_transcript(entries: list[dict], commit_time: datetime, files: set[str], max_steps: int = 40) -> dict:
114	    """Find the request behind a commit made at `commit_time`, and what the agent did about it.
115	
116	    The request is the last prompt a person typed before the commit. A checkpoint can cover
117	    several commits from one long turn, so the commit time is what ties a prompt to a commit.
118	    """
119	    prompts = []
120	    for entry in entries:
121	        text, at = _prompt_text(entry), _when(entry.get("timestamp"))
122	        if text and at and at <= commit_time:
123	            prompts.append((at, text, (entry.get("uuid") or "")[:8]))
124	    if not prompts:
125	        return {"request": None, "earlier_requests": [], "steps": []}
126	    asked_at, request, request_id = prompts[-1]
127	    steps = []
128	    for entry in entries:
129	        at = _when(entry.get("timestamp"))
130	        if entry.get("type") == "assistant" and not entry.get("isSidechain") and at and asked_at <= at <= commit_time:
131	            steps += _steps(entry, files)
132	    # Keep everything that touched the commit's files, and fill the rest with what was said most recently.
133	    keep = [s for s in steps if s.file][-max_steps:]
134	    rest = [s for s in steps if not s.file][-max(0, max_steps - len(keep)):]
135	    order = {id(s): n for n, s in enumerate(steps)}
136	    chosen = sorted(keep + rest, key=lambda s: order[id(s)])
137	    return {
138	        "request": request, "request_id": request_id, "request_time": asked_at.isoformat(),
139	        "earlier_requests": [text for _, text, _ in prompts[:-1]][-5:], "steps": chosen,
140	    }
141	
142	
143	def find_motive(repo: str | Path, sha: str) -> Motive:
144	    """Everything Entire knows about why this commit was made."""
145	    full, subject, stamp, trailer = git(
146	        repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%H%x00%s%x00%cI%x00%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly,separator=%x20)", sha
147	    ).strip().split("\x00")
148	    body = git(repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%b", full)
149	    body = "\n".join(line for line in body.splitlines() if not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z-]+: ", line)).strip()  # drop trailers
150	    motive = Motive(sha=full, subject=subject, link=checkpoint_link(repo, full), message=body)
151	    if not trailer.strip():
152	        motive.note = "This commit has no Entire checkpoint, so there is no recorded request behind it."
153	        return motive
154	    motive.checkpoint = trailer.split()[0]
155	    meta = entire(repo, "checkpoint", "explain", "--checkpoint", motive.checkpoint, "--json")
156	    if meta is None:
157	        motive.note = f"The commit names Entire checkpoint {motive.checkpoint}, and Entire cannot find it, so the request behind this commit is not on record."
158	        return motive
159	    sessions = json.loads(meta).get("sessions") or [{}]
160	    files = {f for f in git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", full).split("\n") if f}
161	    made_at = datetime.fromisoformat(stamp).astimezone(timezone.utc)
162	    # A checkpoint takes in every session that was open in the folder when the commit was made,
163	    # including ones that had nothing to do with it. The session wanted is the one that edited
164	    # the commit's files.
165	    best, best_score, chosen = None, -1.0, 0
166	    for index in range(len(sessions)):
167	        raw = entire(repo, "checkpoint", "explain", "--checkpoint", motive.checkpoint, "--session-index", str(index), "--raw-transcript")
168	        if not raw:
169	            continue
170	        entries = []
171	        for line in raw.splitlines():
172	            try:
173	                entries.append(json.loads(line))
174	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
175	                continue
176	        candidate = read_transcript(entries, made_at, files)
177	        if candidate["request"] is None:
178	            continue
179	        score = sum(1.0 for step in candidate["steps"] if step.kind == "edited") + (0.5 if any(step.kind == "ran" and "ommit" in step.text for step in candidate["steps"]) else 0.0)
180	        if score > best_score:
181	            best, best_score, chosen = candidate, score, index
182	    if best is None:
183	        motive.note = "The checkpoint has no transcript with a prompt from before this commit."
184	        return motive
185	    found = best
186	    motive.session, motive.agent, motive.model = (sessions[chosen].get(k) for k in ("session_id", "agent", "model"))
187	    if len(sessions) > 1:
188	        motive.note = (f"This checkpoint holds {len(sessions)} sessions. " + (
189	            "The one that edited the commit's files was used." if best_score >= 1 else "None of them edited the commit's files, so the request shown may not be the cause of this commit."))
190	    for key, value in found.items():
191	        setattr(motive, key, value)
192	    # A session transcript is full of absolute paths. The case file is public, so they go.
193	    here, home = str(Path(repo).resolve()), str(Path.home())
194	
195	    def scrub(text: str) -> str:
196	        return text.replace(here + "/", "").replace(here, ".").replace(home, "~")
197	
198	    motive.request = scrub(motive.request)
199	    motive.earlier_requests = [scrub(t) for t in motive.earlier_requests]
200	    for step in motive.steps:
201	        step.text = scrub(step.text)
202	    return motive
203

1	"""The root-cause brief.
2	
3	It is written from three things: the culprit's diff, the part of the coding session that
4	produced it, and a failing run set against a passing one. Every sentence has to cite a span id,
5	a commit or a checkpoint that is actually in that evidence, and a sentence that does not is cut.
6	"""
7	
8	import json
9	import re
10	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from . import llm
14	from .motive import Motive
15	from .neat import Mcp, NeatError, replay_runs
16	from .suspects import git
17	
18	MAX_DIFF = 6000
19	
20	
21	@dataclass
22	class Evidence:
23	    culprit: str
24	    parent: str
25	    subject: str
26	    diff: str
27	    after: str = ""  # the changed code as it reads after the commit, with line numbers
28	    checkpoint: str | None = None
29	    request: str | None = None
30	    message: str = ""  # the body of the culprit's commit message
31	    steps: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
32	    failing_run: dict | None = None  # {"trace_id", "commit", "input", "outline"}
33	    passing_run: dict | None = None
34	    comparison: str | None = None
35	    measured: str = ""  # what the lineup measured, in words
36	    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
37	
38	    def citable(self) -> set[str]:
39	        """Every id a sentence may cite."""
40	        ids = {self.culprit[:12], self.parent[:12]}
41	        if self.checkpoint:
42	            ids.add(self.checkpoint)
43	        ids.update(step["id"] for step in self.steps if step.get("id"))
44	        for run in (self.failing_run, self.passing_run):
45	            if run:
46	                ids.add(run["trace_id"][:12])
47	                ids.update(re.findall(r"^\s*([0-9a-f]{8}) [A-Z_]+ ", run.get("outline", ""), flags=re.M))
48	        return ids
49	
50	
51	def _match_run(runs: list[dict], replay: dict, replays: list[dict] = ()) -> dict | None:
52	    """The neatroots run a replay produced, by the replay's own tag when it has one.
53	
54	    Older records have no tags, and for those: same commit, same input, started while the replay
55	    ran. Replays that ran side by side on one commit and one input cannot be told apart by time. If
56	    they all ended the same way it does not matter which is which, and the closest one is taken.
57	    """
58	    if replay.get("tag"):
59	        return next((r for r in runs if r.get("case") == replay["tag"]), None)
60	    start, end = replay["started"] * 1000 - 1500, (replay["started"] + replay["seconds"]) * 1000 + 1500
61	    hits = [r for r in runs if r["commit"] == replay["sha"] and r["input_preview"] == replay["input"] and start <= r["started_ms"] <= end]
62	    if len(hits) == 1:
63	        return hits[0]
64	    if not hits:
65	        return None
66	    beside = [
67	        r for r in replays
68	        if r["sha"] == replay["sha"] and r["input"] == replay["input"]
69	        and r["started"] < replay["started"] + replay["seconds"] and replay["started"] < r["started"] + r["seconds"]
70	    ]
71	    if all(r["verdict"] == replay["verdict"] for r in beside):
72	        return min(hits, key=lambda r: abs(r["started_ms"] - replay["started"] * 1000))
73	    return None
74	
75	
76	def gather(repo: str | Path, case_id: str, culprit: str, target: str, replays: list[dict], motive: Motive | None, mcp: Mcp | None, order: list[str] | None = None) -> Evidence:
77	    """Collect what the brief may draw on. `replays` are the lineup's replays, as dicts.
78	
79	    `order` is the suspects' SHAs oldest first. A failing run is taken from the culprit or the
80	    nearest commit after it, and a passing run from the nearest commit before it, same input.
81	    """
82	    full = git(repo, "rev-parse", culprit).strip()
83	    parent = git(repo, "rev-parse", f"{full}^").strip()
84	    subject = git(repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%s", full).strip()
85	    diff = git(repo, "show", "--format=", "--unified=3", full, "--", target)
86	    if len(diff) > MAX_DIFF:
87	        diff = diff[:MAX_DIFF] + "\n[diff cut here]\n"
88	    evidence = Evidence(culprit=full, parent=parent, subject=subject, diff=diff, after=code_after(repo, full, target))
89	    if motive:
90	        evidence.checkpoint, evidence.request, evidence.message = motive.checkpoint, motive.request, motive.message
91	        evidence.steps = [asdict(s) for s in motive.steps]
92	    if mcp is None:
93	        evidence.notes.append("neatroots was not asked for runs.")
94	        return evidence
95	    try:
96	        runs = replay_runs(mcp, case_id)
97	        order = order or [full]
98	        at = order.index(full) if full in order else 0
99	        rank = {sha: n for n, sha in enumerate(order)}
100	        rank.setdefault(parent, -1)
101	        failing = sorted((r for r in replays if r["verdict"] == "fail" and rank.get(r["sha"], -9) >= at), key=lambda r: rank[r["sha"]])
102	        for replay in failing:
103	            run = _match_run(runs, replay, replays)
104	            if run is None:
105	                continue
106	            passing = sorted(
107	                (r for r in replays if r["verdict"] == "pass" and r["input"] == replay["input"] and -1 <= rank.get(r["sha"], -9) < at),
108	                key=lambda r: -rank[r["sha"]],
109	            )
110	            other = next((m for m in (_match_run(runs, r, replays) for r in passing) if m), None)
111	            evidence.failing_run = {"trace_id": run["trace_id"], "commit": run["commit"], "input": replay["input"], "reason": replay["reason"],
112	                                    "outline": mcp.call("get_run_outline", trace_id=run["trace_id"])["outline"]}
113	            if other:
114	                evidence.passing_run = {"trace_id": other["trace_id"], "commit": other["commit"], "input": replay["input"],
115	                                        "outline": mcp.call("get_run_outline", trace_id=other["trace_id"])["outline"]}
116	                compared = mcp.call("compare_runs", a=other["trace_id"], b=run["trace_id"])
117	                evidence.comparison = compared if isinstance(compared, str) else json.dumps(compared, indent=1)[:3000]
118	            break
119	        if evidence.failing_run is None:
120	            evidence.notes.append("No failing replay could be matched to a run in neatroots.")
121	        elif evidence.passing_run is None:
122	            evidence.notes.append("No passing replay of the same input before the culprit could be matched to a run in neatroots.")
123	    except (NeatError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
124	        evidence.notes.append(f"neatroots could not supply runs: {exc}")
125	    return evidence
126

128	def code_after(repo: str | Path, sha: str, target: str, around: int = 10, limit: int = 4000) -> str:
129	    """The lines each hunk touched, as they read after the commit, numbered and with their indentation intact.
130	
131	    A diff's leading + and - columns make indentation easy to misread, and indentation is often the bug.
132	    """
133	    out = []
134	    names = [f for f in git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", sha, "--", target).split("\n") if f]
135	    for name in names:
136	        try:
137	            lines = git(repo, "show", f"{sha}:{name}").split("\n")
138	        except RuntimeError:
139	            continue  # the commit deleted this file
140	        for start, count in re.findall(r"^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@", git(repo, "show", "--format=", "--unified=0", sha, "--", name), flags=re.M):
141	            first = max(1, int(start) - around)
142	            last = min(len(lines), int(start) + int(count or 1) + around)
143	            out.append(f"{name}, lines {first} to {last} after the commit:\n" + "\n".join(f"{n:>4}  {lines[n - 1]}" for n in range(first, last + 1)))
144	    return "\n\n".join(out)[:limit]
145	
146	
147	SYSTEM = """You write the root-cause brief for a regression in an AI agent. You are given the commit that a bisect \
148	named as the culprit, what the coding agent was asked to do in that commit, and a failing run next to a passing run.
149	
150	Rules:
151	- Say which commit did it and why first. Then say how the failure shows up in the failing run.
152	- Use only what the evidence shows. If the evidence does not show something, do not say it.
153	- Read the diff line by line before describing it, including its indentation. If the bug fails only some of the time, say what in the code or the run makes it intermittent, or say that the evidence does not show why.
154	- Every sentence must cite at least one id from the list of citable ids: a span id, a commit, a checkpoint or a session step.
155	- If the request behind the commit is on record, give one sentence that sets what was asked for against what the commit did, and says where the two part ways. Cite the checkpoint.
156	- Plain words, short sentences, no hype. Seven sentences at most.
157	
158	Answer with JSON only, in this shape:
159	{"headline": "one line, under 90 characters", "sentences": [{"text": "...", "cites": ["id", "id"]}]}"""
160	
161	
162	def prompt_for(evidence: Evidence, symptom: str) -> str:
163	    parts = [
164	        f"Symptom: {symptom}",
165	        f"Culprit commit: {evidence.culprit[:12]} \"{evidence.subject}\" (parent {evidence.parent[:12]})",
166	        f"What the bisect measured: {evidence.measured or 'not recorded'}",
167	        f"Entire checkpoint: {evidence.checkpoint or 'none'}",
168	        f"What the coding agent was asked: {evidence.request or 'not recorded'}",
169	        f"What the commit message says: {evidence.message or 'nothing beyond the subject'}",
170	        "Session steps between that request and the commit:\n" + ("\n".join(
171	            f"[{s['id']}] {s['kind']}{' ' + s['file'] if s.get('file') else ''}: {s['text'][:400]}" for s in evidence.steps[-25:]) or "none recorded"),
172	        "Diff of the culprit commit:\n" + evidence.diff,
173	        "The changed code as it reads after the commit:\n" + (evidence.after or "not available"),
174	    ]
175	    for label, run in (("Failing run", evidence.failing_run), ("Passing run", evidence.passing_run)):
176	        if run:
177	            parts.append(f"{label} {run['trace_id'][:12]} at commit {run['commit'][:12]}, input: {run['input']}\n{run['outline']}")
178	    if evidence.comparison:
179	        parts.append("neatroots comparison, passing run first:\n" + evidence.comparison)
180	    parts.append("Citable ids: " + ", ".join(sorted(evidence.citable())))
181	    return "\n\n".join(parts)
182	
183	
184	def check_citations(brief: dict, evidence: Evidence) -> dict:
185	    """Keep only sentences whose citations are real. A cite matches by prefix in either direction."""
186	    allowed = evidence.citable()
187	
188	    def real(cite: str) -> str | None:
189	        cite = str(cite).strip().strip("[]`")
190	        if len(cite) < 6:
191	            return None
192	        return next((a for a in allowed if a.startswith(cite) or cite.startswith(a)), None)
193	
194	    kept, dropped = [], []
195	    for sentence in brief.get("sentences", []):
196	        cites = sorted({c for c in (real(c) for c in sentence.get("cites", [])) if c})
197	        (kept if cites and sentence.get("text", "").strip() else dropped).append({"text": sentence.get("text", "").strip(), "cites": cites})
198	    return {"headline": str(brief.get("headline", "")).strip(), "sentences": kept, "dropped": [d["text"] for d in dropped]}
199	
200	
201	def template_brief(evidence: Evidence, symptom: str) -> dict:
202	    """A brief with no model: the facts in fixed sentences, each with its citation."""
203	    culprit = evidence.culprit[:12]
204	    sentences = [{"text": f"The failures start at commit {culprit}, \"{evidence.subject}\".", "cites": [culprit]}]
205	    if evidence.request and evidence.checkpoint:
206	        asked = evidence.request.strip().splitlines()[0][:200]
207	        sentences.append({"text": f"That commit came from a coding session that was asked: \"{asked}\"", "cites": [evidence.checkpoint]})
208	    elif evidence.message:
209	        sentences.append({"text": f"No coding session could be read for that commit. Its own message says: \"{evidence.message.splitlines()[0][:200]}\"", "cites": [culprit]})
210	    else:
211	        sentences.append({"text": "No coding session is recorded for that commit, so the request behind it is unknown.", "cites": [culprit]})
212	    if evidence.failing_run:
213	        run = evidence.failing_run
214	        sentences.append({"text": f"In a failing replay of \"{run['input']}\", {run['reason']}.", "cites": [run["trace_id"][:12]]})
215	    if evidence.passing_run:
216	        run = evidence.passing_run
217	        sentences.append({"text": f"The same input passed one step earlier, at commit {run['commit'][:12]}.", "cites": [run["trace_id"][:12], run["commit"][:12]]})
218	    return {"headline": f"{evidence.subject}: {symptom}"[:90], "sentences": sentences, "dropped": [], "model": "none, fixed template"}
219	
220	
221	def write_brief(evidence: Evidence, symptom: str) -> dict:
222	    """Ask the model for the brief and check its citations. Falls back to the template, and says so."""
223	    if llm.choice() == "none":
224	        return template_brief(evidence, symptom)
225	    try:
226	        answer = llm.ask(SYSTEM, prompt_for(evidence, symptom))
227	        found = re.search(r"\{.*\}", answer, flags=re.S)
228	        brief = check_citations(json.loads(found.group(0)), evidence)
229	    except (llm.LlmError, AttributeError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError) as exc:
230	        fallback = template_brief(evidence, symptom)
231	        fallback["model"] = f"none, fixed template (the model step failed: {exc})"
232	        return fallback
233	    if not brief["sentences"]:
234	        fallback = template_brief(evidence, symptom)
235	        fallback["model"] = "none, fixed template (the model's sentences had no valid citations)"
236	        fallback["dropped"] = brief["dropped"]
237	        return fallback
238	    brief["model"] = llm.model_name()
239	    return brief

1	"""The damages: how many runs went bad, and what they cost.
2	
3	Counts come from the traces neatroots holds. The dollar figures are estimates from token
4	counts and a price per million tokens, and are labelled as estimates wherever they appear.
5	Writing them to cfo.ai is a separate step that needs the owner's yes.
6	"""
7	
8	import json
9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
10	
11	from .neat import Mcp, select_all
12	
13	# US dollars per million tokens (input, output), by the model name on the LLM span. These are
14	# list prices as best known when this was written. Pass your own to `count` for real billing.
15	PRICES = {"claude-haiku": (1.00, 5.00), "claude-sonnet-4.6": (3.00, 15.00), "fake": (0.0, 0.0), "mock": (0.0, 0.0)}
16	
17	
18	@dataclass
19	class Damages:
20	    workflow: str
21	    since_ms: float | None
22	    runs: int
23	    bad_runs: int
24	    bad_share: float
25	    tokens: int
26	    bad_tokens: int
27	    cost_usd: float  # of all runs in the window
28	    wasted_usd: float  # of the bad runs
29	    replay_runs: int = 0  # runs Whodunit itself made while investigating
30	    replay_usd: float = 0.0
31	    case_runs: int = 0  # ordinary runs on the culprit or later whose request is one of the case's inputs
32	    case_bad: int = 0  # of those, the ones that paid out something other than what the case expects
33	    wrongly_paid: float = 0.0  # money refunded that should not have been, in the orders' currency
34	    withheld: float = 0.0  # money that should have been refunded and was not
35	    note: str = "Dollar figures are estimates from token counts."
36	
37	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
38	        return asdict(self)
39	
40	
41	def _cost(prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int, price: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
42	    return (prompt_tokens * price[0] + completion_tokens * price[1]) / 1_000_000
43	
44	
45	BAD = "(r.status = 'error' or r.error_count > 0 or r.finding_count > 0)"
46	REPLAY = "exists (select 1 from spans i where i.trace_id = r.trace_id and i.name = 'run_info' and i.attributes like '{like}')"
47	
48	
49	def _spend(mcp: Mcp, where: str, prices: dict) -> tuple[float, float, int, int]:
50	    """(cost of all runs, cost of bad runs, tokens, bad tokens) for the runs that match, priced per model."""
51	    rows = mcp.call("query_sql", sql=(
52	        f"select s.model as model, {BAD} as bad, coalesce(sum(s.prompt_tokens), 0) as pt, coalesce(sum(s.completion_tokens), 0) as ct "
53	        f"from runs r join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.span_kind = 'LLM' where {where} group by s.model, bad"
54	    ))["rows"]
55	    cost = bad_cost = tokens = bad_tokens = 0
56	    for row in rows:
57	        spent = _cost(row["pt"], row["ct"], prices.get(row["model"] or "", (0.0, 0.0)))
58	        cost, tokens = cost + spent, tokens + row["pt"] + row["ct"]
59	        if row["bad"]:
60	            bad_cost, bad_tokens = bad_cost + spent, bad_tokens + row["pt"] + row["ct"]
61	    return cost, bad_cost, tokens, bad_tokens
62	
63	
64	def count(mcp: Mcp, workflow: str, commits: list[str] | None = None, since_ms: float | None = None, case_id: str | None = None,
65	          prices: dict | None = None) -> Damages:
66	    """Count the workflow's ordinary runs on the culprit and the commits after it.
67	
68	    `commits` are those SHAs. A run is bad if it errored or neatroots raised a finding on it.
69	    Replays made for a case are left out of the damage and reported on their own line.
70	    """
71	    prices = prices or PRICES
72	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
73	    window = f" and r.started_ms >= {float(since_ms)}" if since_ms else ""
74	    production = f"r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0{window} and not " + REPLAY.format(like="%case:%")
75	    if commits is not None:
76	        on_bad = " or ".join(f"i.attributes like '%commit:{sha}%'" for sha in commits if sha.isalnum()) or "0"
77	        production += f" and exists (select 1 from spans i where i.trace_id = r.trace_id and i.name = 'run_info' and ({on_bad}))"
78	    row = mcp.call("query_sql", sql=f"select count(*) as runs, coalesce(sum({BAD}), 0) as bad from runs r where {production}")["rows"][0]
79	    cost, bad_cost, tokens, bad_tokens = _spend(mcp, production, prices)
80	    damages = Damages(
81	        workflow=workflow, since_ms=since_ms, runs=row["runs"], bad_runs=row["bad"],
82	        bad_share=round(row["bad"] / row["runs"], 4) if row["runs"] else 0.0,
83	        tokens=tokens, bad_tokens=bad_tokens, cost_usd=round(cost, 4), wasted_usd=round(bad_cost, 4),
84	    )
85	    if case_id:
86	        mine = REPLAY.format(like=f"%case:{case_id}%".replace("'", "''"))
87	        damages.replay_runs = mcp.call("query_sql", sql=f"select count(*) as runs from runs r where {mine}")["rows"][0]["runs"]
88	        damages.replay_usd = round(_spend(mcp, mine, prices)[0], 4)
89	    return damages
90	
91	
92	def count_case(mcp: Mcp, damages: Damages, workflow: str, commits: list[str], inputs: list[tuple[str, list[dict]]]) -> Damages:
93	    """Judge the ordinary runs that asked exactly what the case asks, and add up the money.
94	
95	    `inputs` are (request text, refunds a correct run pays). What a run paid is read from its
96	    issue_refund tool spans. This is the part of the damage that is in the shop's currency and
97	    not in tokens: refunds that went out wrongly, and refunds that should have and did not.
98	    """
99	    expected = {text: {str(r["order_id"]): float(r["refunded"]) for r in refunds} for text, refunds in inputs}
100	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
101	    on_bad = " or ".join(f"i.attributes like '%commit:{sha}%'" for sha in commits if sha.isalnum()) or "0"
102	    asked = ", ".join("'" + text.replace("'", "''") + "'" for text in expected) or "''"
103	    runs = select_all(mcp, (
104	        "select r.trace_id, r.input_preview from runs r where "
105	        f"r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0 and r.input_preview in ({asked}) and not " + REPLAY.format(like="%case:%") +
106	        f" and exists (select 1 from spans i where i.trace_id = r.trace_id and i.name = 'run_info' and ({on_bad}))"
107	    ), cap=1000)
108	    if not runs:
109	        return damages
110	    ids = ", ".join("'" + r["trace_id"] + "'" for r in runs)
111	    paid: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {r["trace_id"]: {} for r in runs}
112	    for span in select_all(mcp, f"select trace_id, output_preview from spans where name = 'issue_refund' and status_code != 2 and trace_id in ({ids})"):
113	        try:
114	            out = json.loads(span["output_preview"] or "{}")
115	            order, amount = str(out["order_id"]), float(out["refunded"])
116	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
117	            continue
118	        paid[span["trace_id"]][order] = paid[span["trace_id"]].get(order, 0.0) + amount
119	    for run in runs:
120	        want, got = expected[run["input_preview"]], paid[run["trace_id"]]
121	        over = sum(max(0.0, got.get(o, 0.0) - want.get(o, 0.0)) for o in set(got) | set(want))
122	        under = sum(max(0.0, want.get(o, 0.0) - got.get(o, 0.0)) for o in set(got) | set(want))
123	        damages.case_runs += 1
124	        if over > 0.005 or under > 0.005:
125	            damages.case_bad += 1
126	            damages.wrongly_paid += over
127	            damages.withheld += under
128	    damages.wrongly_paid, damages.withheld = round(damages.wrongly_paid, 2), round(damages.withheld, 2)

1	"""The onset: when did the failures begin, and between which commits?
2	
3	Every run of the agent carries the commit it ran on. Ordinary traffic therefore already says
4	a good deal about the culprit before any replay is spent: this module reads those runs from
5	neatroots, and uses the same change-point model as the lineup to find where the failures start.
6	"""
7	
8	import json
9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
10	
11	from .lineup import ChangePoint
12	from .neat import Mcp, select_all
13	
14	
15	@dataclass
16	class Onset:
17	    workflow: str
18	    commits: list[dict]  # in order of first appearance: {"sha", "first_seen_ms", "runs", "bad"}
19	    good: str | None = None  # last commit that is very unlikely to be at or after the change
20	    bad: str | None = None  # newest commit seen
21	    likeliest: str | None = None  # the single most likely first bad commit, from traffic alone
22	    probability: float = 0.0
23	    first_failure_ms: float | None = None  # first bad run at or after the likeliest commit
24	    bad_runs: int = 0
25	    runs: int = 0
26	    failing_inputs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
27	    note: str = ""
28	
29	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
30	        return asdict(self)
31	
32	
33	def traffic(mcp: Mcp, workflow: str, limit: int = 5000) -> list[dict]:
34	    """The workflow's ordinary runs, oldest first, each with its commit. Whodunit's own replays are left out."""
35	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
36	    rows = select_all(mcp, (
37	        "select r.trace_id, r.started_ms, r.input_preview, s.output_preview as info, "
38	        "(r.status = 'error' or r.error_count > 0 or r.finding_count > 0) as bad "
39	        "from runs r join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.name = 'run_info' "
40	        f"where r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0 and s.attributes not like '%case:%' order by r.started_ms"
41	    ), cap=limit)
42	    out = []
43	    for row in rows:
44	        try:
45	            tags = json.loads(row.pop("info") or "{}").get("tags", [])
46	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError):
47	            continue
48	        commit = next((t.split(":", 1)[1] for t in tags if t.startswith("commit:")), None)
49	        if commit and commit != "unknown":
50	            out.append({**row, "commit": commit, "bad": bool(row["bad"])})
51	    return out
52	
53	
54	def find_onset(workflow: str, runs: list[dict], floor: float = 0.01) -> Onset:
55	    """Where the failures begin, given runs as {"commit", "started_ms", "bad", "input_preview"}, oldest first.
56	
57	    Commits are ordered by when they were first seen. The oldest commit is taken as the baseline.
58	    The good ref is the last commit before the change point's posterior reaches `floor`, so the
59	    range handed to the lineup is wide enough to hold the culprit.
60	    """
61	    order: dict[str, dict] = {}
62	    for run in runs:
63	        seen = order.setdefault(run["commit"], {"sha": run["commit"], "first_seen_ms": run["started_ms"], "runs": 0, "bad": 0})
64	        seen["runs"] += 1
65	        seen["bad"] += run["bad"]
66	    commits = list(order.values())
67	    onset = Onset(workflow=workflow, commits=commits, runs=len(runs), bad_runs=sum(r["bad"] for r in runs))
68	    if len(commits) < 2:
69	        onset.note = "Runs from at least two commits are needed to place the onset."
70	        return onset
71	    if onset.bad_runs == 0:
72	        onset.note = "No bad runs in the traffic."
73	        return onset
74	    state = ChangePoint(len(commits) - 1)  # the oldest commit plays the good ref
75	    for position, commit in enumerate(commits):
76	        for _ in range(commit["bad"]):
77	            state.observe(position - 1, True)
78	        for _ in range(commit["runs"] - commit["bad"]):
79	            state.observe(position - 1, False)
80	    posterior = state.posterior()
81	    top = max(range(len(posterior)), key=posterior.__getitem__)
82	    mass, start = 0.0, 0
83	    for i, share in enumerate(posterior):
84	        mass += share
85	        if mass >= floor:
86	            start = i
87	            break
88	    onset.good = commits[start]["sha"]  # suspect i is commits[i + 1], so the commit before suspect `start` is commits[start]
89	    onset.bad = commits[-1]["sha"]
90	    onset.likeliest, onset.probability = commits[top + 1]["sha"], round(posterior[top], 4)
91	    since = commits[top + 1]["first_seen_ms"]
92	    later_bad = [r for r in runs if r["bad"] and r["started_ms"] >= since]
93	    onset.first_failure_ms = later_bad[0]["started_ms"] if later_bad else None
94	    inputs: dict[str, int] = {}
95	    for run in later_bad:
96	        if run.get("input_preview"):
97	            inputs[run["input_preview"]] = inputs.get(run["input_preview"], 0) + 1
98	    onset.failing_inputs = sorted(inputs, key=lambda text: -inputs[text])[:5]
99	    return onset
100	
101	
102	def cloud_trend(detection: str = "Execution Failed") -> dict:
103	    """Ask neatlogs cloud when a detection started firing. Needs NEATLOGS_API_KEY in .env.
104	
105	    Returns {"detection", "first_seen", "total", "points"}, where first_seen is the start of the
106	    first bucket with any occurrences, or None if the detection has not fired in the period.
107	    """
108	    import os
109	
110	    from .env import load_env
111	    from .neat import NEATLOGS
112	
113	    load_env()
114	    key = os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "")
115	    if not key:
116	        raise RuntimeError("NEATLOGS_API_KEY is not in .env")
117	    trend = Mcp(NEATLOGS, token=key).call("get_detection_trend", detection_name=detection)
118	    points = trend.get("data_points", [])
119	    first = next((p["date"] for p in points if p.get("count", 0) > 0), None)
120	    return {"detection": trend.get("detection_name", detection), "first_seen": first, "total": trend.get("total_occurrences", 0), "points": points}
121	
122	
123	def witness(mcp: Mcp, workflow: str, positions: dict[str, int], inputs: list[tuple[str, list[dict]]]) -> list[tuple[int, bool]]:
124	    """What ordinary traffic already says about a case, as (position, failed) pairs for the lineup.
125	
126	    `positions` maps a commit to its place in the lineup (-1 for the good ref). A run counts when
127	    it asked exactly what one of the case's inputs asks, and it failed if what it refunded is not
128	    what the case expects. These runs were already paid for, so they cost the lineup nothing.
129	    """
130	    expected = {text: {str(r["order_id"]): float(r["refunded"]) for r in refunds} for text, refunds in inputs}
131	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
132	    asked = ", ".join("'" + text.replace("'", "''") + "'" for text in expected) or "''"
133	    rows = select_all(mcp, (
134	        "select r.trace_id, r.input_preview, s.output_preview as info from runs r "
135	        "join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.name = 'run_info' "
136	        f"where r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0 and r.input_preview in ({asked}) and s.attributes not like '%case:%' "
137	        "order by r.started_ms desc"
138	    ), cap=1000)
139	    runs = []
140	    for row in rows:
141	        try:
142	            tags = json.loads(row["info"] or "{}").get("tags", [])
143	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError):
144	            continue
145	        commit = next((t.split(":", 1)[1] for t in tags if t.startswith("commit:")), None)
146	        if commit in positions:
147	            runs.append((row["trace_id"], row["input_preview"], positions[commit]))
148	    if not runs:
149	        return []
150	    ids = ", ".join("'" + trace + "'" for trace, _, _ in runs)
151	    paid: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {trace: {} for trace, _, _ in runs}
152	    for span in select_all(mcp, f"select trace_id, output_preview from spans where name = 'issue_refund' and status_code != 2 and trace_id in ({ids})"):
153	        try:
154	            out = json.loads(span["output_preview"] or "{}")
155	            order, amount = str(out["order_id"]), float(out["refunded"])
156	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
157	            continue
158	        paid[span["trace_id"]][order] = paid[span["trace_id"]].get(order, 0.0) + amount
159	    evidence = []
160	    for trace, text, position in runs:
161	        want, got = expected[text], paid[trace]
162	        wrong = any(abs(got.get(o, 0.0) - want.get(o, 0.0)) > 0.005 for o in set(got) | set(want))
163	        evidence.append((position, wrong))
164	    return evidence

24	
25	Replay spend on the gateway, estimated from token counts at list prices, came to about $1.91 for all five cases:
26	
27	- cents-off: about $0.08 (61,267 tokens)
28	- wrong-order-refunded: about $0.57 (438,034 tokens)
29	- half-done-batch: about $1.04 (795,110 tokens)
30	- strangers-paid: about $0.10 (78,530 tokens)
31	- turned-away: about $0.12 (100,111 tokens)
32	
33	## What this does and does not show
34	
35	- No commit was wrongly accused, at either budget. On `half-done-batch` the top suspect at 120 replays was the wrong commit, at 53%, and Whodunit named nobody. That is the behaviour the 95% bar is for.
36	- The two cases it could not close at 120 replays are the two that fail least often. Whodunit put them at 12% and 14%, where the second session had measured 30% and 25% from a handful of probes. A bug that rare needs a lot of replays whatever the method.
37	- The ranges are short, 11 to 15 suspects. On ranges this size a careful scan from the oldest commit would have replayed about as many commits as Whodunit did, so this eval says little about savings on long histories. The simulator in `eval/simulator` covers 40 suspects.
38	- Five cases is a small sample. It is enough to say the pipeline works on a history it did not write, and not enough to put a number on accuracy.
39	- Each case has one planted regression inside its range, by design. Two regressions that touch the same inputs in one range are outside what the model assumes.
40	
41	## What happened after the culprits were named
42	
43	The owner's ruling was patch for all three kinds of change involved. A fix counts as proven when its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit, at 95%.
44	
45	| Case | Outcome | Tries | Replays of the final fix |
46	| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
47	| cents-off | patched and proven | 1 | 0 failures in 30 |
48	| strangers-paid | patched and proven | 1 | 0 failures in 30 |
49	| wrong-order-refunded | patched and proven | 1 | 0 failures in 36 |
50	| turned-away | two patches not proven, then reverted and proven | 3 | 0 failures in 30 |
51	| half-done-batch | not fixed | 3 | two patches left 5 failures in 90 each, and the revert conflicts |
52	
53	So four of five were closed, one of them only by giving up on the patch the owner asked for, and one was left open and says so.
54	
55	## The same culprit across the whole history
56	
57	`cases/whole-history.toml` takes the `strangers-paid` regression and widens the range to the whole grown history, 57 suspects. With alibis from entire-graph for 22 of them and 18 ordinary runs as evidence, 20 replays across 5 commits named the culprit at 99.8%. A scan from the oldest suspect would have tested 37 commits. This is the run that speaks to savings on a longer history, and it is one run.
58	
59	## Against plain bisect with retries
60	
61	The same five cases were then given to plain bisect, with each commit replayed up to 5 times over and called bad on the first failure. It ran once per case, so this is one sample and not a rate.
62	
63	| Case | Plain bisect, 5 retries | Its replays | Statistical bisect | Its replays |
64	| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
65	| cents-off | right | 15 | right | 21 |
66	| strangers-paid | right | 15 | right | 30 |
67	| turned-away | right | 25 | right | 24 |
68	| wrong-order-refunded | wrong commit named | 19 | right | 168 |
69	| half-done-batch | could not start: the bad ref passed 10 replays in a row | 10 | right | 168 |
70	
71	On the three bugs that fail most of the time, plain bisect was right and used 55 replays in all against 75. That matches the simulator: with a clean baseline, and this one was clean (0 failures in 211 replays of commits before a culprit), plain bisect with retries is the cheaper tool.
72	
73	On the two bugs that fail about one run in eight, it went wrong in the two ways it can. For `wrong-order-refunded` a bad commit passed all 5 tries, the search went the wrong way, and it named an innocent commit three places from the real one, with nothing to say it was unsure. For `half-done-batch` the bad ref itself passed 10 replays in a row, so there was nothing to bisect.
74	
75	More retries would have fixed both, at a cost. The trouble is that the number has to be picked before the failure rate is known. The statistical bisect does not need it picked: it spent 21 to 30 replays on the frequent bugs and 168 on the rare ones, and on the rare ones it said "not sure yet" at 120 instead of naming someone.
76	# Simulator results
77	
78	How often does the lineup name the right commit, for a given number of replays? This folder answers that with simulated cases, where the culprit is known.
79	
80	Each case has 40 suspect commits and one culprit picked at random. Every point is 500 cases. Three methods get the same cases and the same replay budget:
81	
82	- The statistical bisect in `whodunit/lineup.py`. It names a commit only when it is 95% sure, and otherwise hands back the suspects that remain with their probabilities.
83	- Plain bisect with repeats. It replays each commit as many times as the budget allows and calls the commit bad on the first failure.
84	- Plain bisect with one replay per commit, which is what `git bisect run` does.
85	
86	To regenerate everything here, run `uv run python -m whodunit.simulate --out eval/simulator`. It takes about two minutes. `tables.md` has every number behind the charts, and `results.json` has the raw counts.
87	
88	## When good commits never fail
89	
90	![Accuracy against replay budget when good commits never fail](accuracy-clean-baseline.svg)
91	
92	Plain bisect with repeats wins here at every budget. For a bug that fails 30% of the time, 80 replays get it to 97% while the statistical bisect names the right commit in 67% of cases. The statistical bisect needs 160 replays to reach 93%.
93	
94	The reason is that plain bisect with repeats assumes a single failure convicts a commit, and in this world that is true. The statistical bisect does not assume it. It starts out believing a good commit fails about 5% of the time and spends replays finding out.
95	
96	Two things are worth knowing before picking plain bisect on that basis. Its mistakes are silent: with 40 replays on the 30% bug it names the wrong commit in 26% of cases and gives no sign of it, where the statistical bisect names the wrong one in 2% and says "not sure yet" in the rest. And the dashed line shows the statistical bisect's top suspect is right in 91% of cases at 80 replays, so most of its "not sure yet" answers are pointing at the culprit already.
97	
98	Plain bisect with one replay per commit is right 10% of the time on the 30% bug, at any budget.
99	
100	## When good commits fail 5% of the time on their own
101	
102	![Accuracy against replay budget when good commits fail 5% of the time](accuracy-flaky-baseline.svg)
103	
104	Agents are rarely this clean. Give every good commit a 5% chance of failing by itself and plain bisect with repeats falls apart, and more replays make it worse. On the 30% bug it is right in 31% of cases with 40 replays and 4% with 320, because every extra replay of an innocent commit is another chance for a stray failure to convict it. Even a bug that fails every time is found in only 46% of cases at 40 replays.
105	
106	The statistical bisect holds up. On the 30% bug it names the right commit in 60% of cases with 160 replays and 84% with 320. On a bug that fails every time it is right in 99% of cases and uses about 21 replays.
107	
108	## Where it falls short
109	
110	- A bug that fails 20% of the time on a flaky baseline is named in only 46% of cases, even with 320 replays. The top suspect is right in 70%.
111	- The 95% bar is not always met. Across the cells, the share of cases with a wrong accusation runs from 0% to 7%, and the 7% is the 30% bug on a flaky baseline at 320 replays. The model assumes one change point and two fixed failure rates, and the prior on the good rate is a guess.
112	- These are simulated commits with independent replays. Real replays share a model provider and a machine, so their failures can come in bursts, which this does not capture.
113	- Small budgets are spent mostly on warming up. Below about 30 replays the statistical bisect rarely names anyone unless the bug fails every time.
114	
115	## What changed from the first design
116	
117	Two things, both found by simulating the 30% bug across 40 suspects with 300 replays allowed.
118	
119	The first version put a uniform prior on both failure rates, so it had to learn from scratch that good commits mostly pass. It solved 59% of cases. Starting from the belief that a good commit fails about 5% of the time, loosely held, took that to 93%.
120	
121	The brief said to test the commit that splits the posterior mass most evenly. The code now defaults to the replay with the highest expected information gain, and keeps the even split as `how="split"`. With the uniform prior the difference was large, 92% against 59%. With the current prior it is small: 282 cases solved against 280 out of 300, using 79 replays on average against 83. So the prior did the work, and the choice of picker barely matters.

123	
124	Generated by `python -m whodunit.simulate`. The charts in this folder draw the same numbers.
125	
126	## Good commits never fail.

131	
132	| Replays allowed | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 60 | 80 | 120 | 160 | 240 | 320 |

python3 - <<'EOF'
import json,glob
for p in sorted(glob.glob('cases/*.record.json')):
    r=json.load(open(p))
    print('=====',p, list(r.keys()))
    l=r.get('lineup',{})
    print({k:v for k,v in l.items() if k not in('remaining',)})
    print('remaining', l.get('remaining'))
    reps=r.get('replays',[])
    from collections import Counter
    order={s['sha']:i for i,s in enumerate(r['suspects'])}
    c=Counter((order.get(x['sha'],-1),x['verdict']) for x in reps)
    print('replays total',len(reps), sorted(c.items()))
    print('reasons sample', Counter(x['reason'][:60] for x in reps if x['verdict']=='fail').most_common(5))
    print('alibi count', sum(1 for s in r['suspects'] if s.get('alibi')), Counter(s.get('alibi','')[:50] for s in r['suspects']).most_common(8))
    print('top probs', sorted(((round(s.get('probability',0),4),i) for i,s in enumerate(r['suspects'])),reverse=True)[:4])
    print('ruling', r.get('ruling'))
    for a in r.get('attempts',[]):
        print('attempt', a.get('kind'), a.get('commit'), a.get('note'), a.get('verification'), a.get('failed_replays'))
    print('fix', {k:v for k,v in (r.get('fix') or {}).items() if k not in('diff',)})
    print('damages', r.get('damages'))
    print('log', r.get('log'))
    print('checks', r.get('checks'))
    m=r.get('motive') or {}
    print('motive', {k:(v if k not in('steps','earlier_requests') else len(v)) for k,v in m.items()})
    b=r.get('brief') or {}
    print('brief', json.dumps(b,indent=1)[:2500])
EOF
